Good morning, all -
So, I have my county equalization and apportionment spreadsheet basically done, just waiting until our public hearing and adoption of the county's budget to get the levy. SCAR decisions are done for this year,

not the judge.
So, I am trying to track down an official signed order.
It got me to thinking though... Do you have a cut-off date that you will make changes to your file for Article 7 or SCAR decisions when working on town & county processing? It would be great to get the correct

Meghan.

Good morning -
I have a follow-up question related to a question I had asked previously.
The backstory - A property owner had requested via a parcel combo form for my tax mapper to combine two adjacent parcels, and she denied it twice because the ownership was not the same.
On parcel A - The son is the sole owner. On parcel B - The son is the owner and the mother has Life Use.
Now the son filed a deed stating that the intention of the deed is to merge the two parcels.
So, my previous question was - Would you merge them? The lawyer is pushing the issue looking for tax law for why we can't.
At the time of my question, one of you (thank you) sent me this Op of Counsel
Volume 5 - Opinions of Counsel SBEA No. 118
How I read that is that the assessor could make the determination whether to allow the parcels to be merged on the role, though this would be for assisting with assessing and tax bill purposes, and NOT in
determination of legal ownership. Ok... fine with that.
Now the lawyer states that the intention is also for the mother's Life Use to carry to the newly MERGED parcel, even though it states nothing about her extending Life Use in the deed to the newly merged parcel.
In fact, she is not mentioned in the deed and did not sign it.
On top of that, the parcel with the house is NOT currently the one the mother has Life Use on. Instead, the son lives there and has a Basic STAR on it. (The other parcel is a vacant lot.)
Would you put the Life Use on the new parcel? The only thing that the new deed states is that the FATHER's Life Use was extinguished because he passed away, but nothing about the mother's life use.
Even if it was put on, and if the mother is living there, too - and if she applied for an Enhanced STAR, it would have to be a credit, not an exemption. What a cluster.
I would appreciated any thoughts. This lawyer is being... persistent.
Thank you and Happy Halloween!!!
~ Meghan.

On Fri, Nov 21, 2025 at 4:17 PM Corey Metz <Corey.Metz@oswegocountyny.gov> wrote:
Law reference time! I'll put the paragraph the language is in before the link.
Village taxes: sent to County within 15 days of end of village tax collection (4.(a)
NYS Open Legislation | NYSenate.gov)
School taxes: sent to County not later than November 15th (2.
NYS Open Legislation | NYSenate.gov)
Unpaid water/sewer: Town law 198 covers a lot of topics but Water (3(d)
NYS Open Legislation | NYSenate.gov) specifically says that no later than November 1st the town clerk must file with the Supervisor a list of unpaid water accounts and the supervisor shall then transmit such statements to "the board of supervisors
of the county at its next regular meeting"
Alternatively what I do: just make your life easy and say everything needs to be submitted at the same time the Town budget is submitted to the County. Towns have until November
20th to pass a budget (NYS Open Legislation | NYSenate.gov), the Town Clerk must deliver within 5 day the final budget to the Town Supervisor (NYS
Open Legislation | NYSenate.gov), and the Town Supervisor must send the budget to the County within 10 days of receiving it from the Clerk (NYS Open Legislation | NYSenate.gov).
So - at the end of the day, December 5th is the absolute latest a town can submit their budget to the County and the budget should include the amounts to be raised for any relevies to be added to tax bills.

Hi everyone,
We have a property where a portion of vacant land was sold in September 2024. Due to an error with the deed/survey map, the subdivision was not processed
in our system in time for the taxable status date, so the parcel was not split on the 2025 assessment roll. As a result:
The new owner of the subdivided portion has not received a school tax bill.
The previous owner of the original parcel is being taxed on the entire acreage.
I'm looking for guidance on the best way to handle this. My current thinking is to file an RP-556 to refund the original owner for the school taxes. At
this point, I would prefer not to make any changes to the roll before the town/county bills so I would also do a correction afterward for original owner to the town/county tax roll. Would the proper approach then be to treat the amount the new owner should
have paid as omits next year?
Thank you!

subject: 65% and worksheet
body:
Good morning,
For anyone who passed a resolution for the 65% senior exemption--were you planning on using the worksheet?
Have you considered workarounds yet? ORPTS wants us to wipe out the worksheet entirely for any affected parcels and update each one manually, but with upwards of 8,000 parcels to be reviewed in Onondaga County between the
towns and City of Syracuse, AND only having the county with this change (so it will mean deleting one and adding 2 new exemptions for towns that use the same income limit as the county, just don't have the bonus 15%), it's not feasible to manually review each
one. Most of our assessors use the worksheet, so that was our plan (and assessors who don't use it had already talked to me ahead of time).
I might be able to "back door" update things, but it will be a significant lift, so if someone else has better ideas, I am all ears.
Thanks,
Kate
Kathleen Kearney, Director
Real Property Tax Services
Onondaga County

Syracuse, New York 13202

On Fri, Nov 21, 2025 at 4:17 PM Corey Metz <Corey.Metz@oswegocountyny.gov> wrote:
Law reference time! I'll put the paragraph the language is in before the link.
Village taxes: sent to County within 15 days of end of village tax collection (4.(a)
NYS Open Legislation | NYSenate.gov)
School taxes: sent to County not later than November 15th (2.
NYS Open Legislation | NYSenate.gov)
Unpaid water/sewer: Town law 198 covers a lot of topics but Water (3(d)
NYS Open Legislation | NYSenate.gov) specifically says that no later than November 1st the town clerk must file with the Supervisor a list of unpaid water accounts and the supervisor shall then transmit such statements to "the board of supervisors
of the county at its next regular meeting"
Alternatively what I do: just make your life easy and say everything needs to be submitted at the same time the Town budget is submitted to the County. Towns have until November
20th to pass a budget (NYS Open Legislation | NYSenate.gov), the Town Clerk must deliver within 5 day the final budget to the Town Supervisor (NYS
Open Legislation | NYSenate.gov), and the Town Supervisor must send the budget to the County within 10 days of receiving it from the Clerk (NYS Open Legislation | NYSenate.gov).
So - at the end of the day, December 5th is the absolute latest a town can submit their budget to the County and the budget should include the amounts to be raised for any relevies to be added to tax bills.

Good morning -
I have a follow-up question related to a question I had asked previously.
The backstory - A property owner had requested via a parcel combo form for my tax mapper to combine two adjacent parcels, and she denied it twice because the ownership was not the same.
On parcel A - The son is the sole owner. On parcel B - The son is the owner and the mother has Life Use.
Now the son filed a deed stating that the intention of the deed is to merge the two parcels.
So, my previous question was - Would you merge them? The lawyer is pushing the issue looking for tax law for why we can't.
At the time of my question, one of you (thank you) sent me this Op of Counsel
Volume 5 - Opinions of Counsel SBEA No. 118
How I read that is that the assessor could make the determination whether to allow the parcels to be merged on the role, though this would be for assisting with assessing and tax bill purposes, and NOT in
determination of legal ownership. Ok... fine with that.
Now the lawyer states that the intention is also for the mother's Life Use to carry to the newly MERGED parcel, even though it states nothing about her extending Life Use in the deed to the newly merged parcel.
In fact, she is not mentioned in the deed and did not sign it.
On top of that, the parcel with the house is NOT currently the one the mother has Life Use on. Instead, the son lives there and has a Basic STAR on it. (The other parcel is a vacant lot.)
Would you put the Life Use on the new parcel? The only thing that the new deed states is that the FATHER's Life Use was extinguished because he passed away, but nothing about the mother's life use.
Even if it was put on, and if the mother is living there, too - and if she applied for an Enhanced STAR, it would have to be a credit, not an exemption. What a cluster.
I would appreciated any thoughts. This lawyer is being... persistent.
Thank you and Happy Halloween!!!
~ Meghan.

senders or unexpected emails.
We have a situation where a town sold their town garage property in December 2024 to a not-for-profit company who rents the land to an adjacent shed company for display space. No exemptions were filed, so the property
was put back onto the tax rolls.
NOW, after not paying school taxes either, the town filed a correction stating that the town-owned property exemption should not have been removed, because the property is still town-owned. Well, sort of. Apparently
(though the assessor at the time was not aware) this not-for-profit company is solely owned by the town as a redevelopment initiative. The certificate of incorporation states that it must be totally separate from the town. This is not considered an "IDA enumerated
in the general municipal law" (per RPTL §412-a), it's just a company that the town created, probably to protect their budgets/finances from the risk/reward of property investments in the town. We asked them for more information from the assessor, so they filed
an exemption under 420-b on 2/17 and expected that to cover them for 2026 county/town taxes.
It's only $1650, but still...what would y'all do? It's not my call to determine exemption eligibility for this roll year, but for a correction almost a year after when they should have applied for their exemption
just because they "didn't know" they'd lose their existing exemption?
Thanks y'all!
Kathleen Kearney, Director
Real Property Tax Services
Onondaga County
421 Montgomery St, 15th Floor
Syracuse, New York 13202
www.ongov.net/RPTS
P: (315) 435-2426

subject: Re: merging parcels
body:
We would not consolidate.  This has happen to us in the past as we did consolidate then the life use questioned why we did so we hold that all have to be in title of all parcels.
Larry F. Roach Jr.
Director
Real Property Tax Service Agency
Steuben County Office Building
3 East Pulteney Sq; Bath NY  14810
Direct Phone: (607) 664-2380
Office Phone: (607) 664-2373
lroach@steubencountyny.gov
From: Real Property Tax Directors <RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US>
On Behalf Of Meghan Kincaid
Sent: Friday, October 31, 2025 11:53 AM
To: RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US
Subject: merging parcels
Good morning -
I have a follow-up question related to a question I had asked previously.
The backstory - A property owner had requested via a parcel combo form for my tax mapper to combine two adjacent parcels, and she denied it twice because the ownership was not the same.
On parcel A - The son is the sole owner. On parcel B - The son is the owner and the mother has Life Use.
Now the son filed a deed stating that the intention of the deed is to merge the two parcels.
So, my previous question was - Would you merge them? The lawyer is pushing the issue looking for tax law for why we can't.
At the time of my question, one of you (thank you) sent me this Op of Counsel
Volume 5 - Opinions of Counsel SBEA No. 118
How I read that is that the assessor could make the determination whether to allow the parcels to be merged on the role, though this would be for assisting with assessing and tax bill purposes, and NOT in
determination of legal ownership. Ok... fine with that.
Now the lawyer states that the intention is also for the mother's Life Use to carry to the newly MERGED parcel, even though it states nothing about her extending Life Use in the deed to the newly merged parcel.
In fact, she is not mentioned in the deed and did not sign it.
On top of that, the parcel with the house is NOT currently the one the mother has Life Use on. Instead, the son lives there and has a Basic STAR on it. (The other parcel is a vacant lot.)
Would you put the Life Use on the new parcel? The only thing that the new deed states is that the FATHER's Life Use was extinguished because he passed away, but nothing about the mother's life use.
Even if it was put on, and if the mother is living there, too - and if she applied for an Enhanced STAR, it would have to be a credit, not an exemption. What a cluster.
I would appreciated any thoughts. This lawyer is being... persistent.
Thank you and Happy Halloween!!!
~ Meghan.
Meghan K. Kincaid

body:
Yeah, the min incomes should be even numbers except the $50,000.01. Our sliding scale is not the same as that (we just set the max incomes at our legislature, so our minimums are, effectively, $47,000/$48,000/49,000).
Though, if I remember correctly, the law for the new local option says that the 50% exemption only goes to people whose income is
less than "M" (in our case, $50,000). So the max income for 50% in our case is now $49,999.999. It's not "equal to or less than."

STOP | THINK | ACT
External email detected. Do not click on links or open attachments from unknown sources. Be alert for phishing attempts & report suspicious email IT Security.
Good morning -
I have a follow-up question related to a question I had asked previously.
The backstory - A property owner had requested via a parcel combo form for my tax mapper to combine two adjacent parcels, and she denied it twice because the ownership was not the same.
On parcel A - The son is the sole owner. On parcel B - The son is the owner and the mother has Life Use.
Now the son filed a deed stating that the intention of the deed is to merge the two parcels.
So, my previous question was - Would you merge them? The lawyer is pushing the issue looking for tax law for why we can't.
At the time of my question, one of you (thank you) sent me this Op of Counsel
Volume 5 - Opinions of Counsel SBEA No. 118
How I read that is that the assessor could make the determination whether to allow the parcels to be merged on the role, though this would be for assisting with assessing and tax bill purposes, and NOT in
determination of legal ownership. Ok... fine with that.
Now the lawyer states that the intention is also for the mother's Life Use to carry to the newly MERGED parcel, even though it states nothing about her extending Life Use in the deed to the newly merged parcel.
In fact, she is not mentioned in the deed and did not sign it.
On top of that, the parcel with the house is NOT currently the one the mother has Life Use on. Instead, the son lives there and has a Basic STAR on it. (The other parcel is a vacant lot.)
Would you put the Life Use on the new parcel? The only thing that the new deed states is that the FATHER's Life Use was extinguished because he passed away, but nothing about the mother's life use.
Even if it was put on, and if the mother is living there, too - and if she applied for an Enhanced STAR, it would have to be a credit, not an exemption. What a cluster.
I would appreciated any thoughts. This lawyer is being... persistent.
Thank you and Happy Halloween!!!
~ Meghan.

body:
Just as an FYI for towns, the town has to pass a local law to allow demolition costs to be added as a charge on the tax bill. Lawn mowing/cleanup costs do not need a local law. We require a
cover sheet for reporting all re-levies to us which I highly recommend because otherwise they can send you a bunch of random bills and will say "relevy these please!" without even a hint of what the total is supposed to be.

subject: Re: [External] merging parcels
body:
My thoughts-i would merge the lots on the tax map. For us that has no bearing on the zoning. I would not put life use on the new parcel-that has to be stated explicity in the deed. gary
From: Real Property Tax Directors <RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US> on behalf of Meghan Kincaid <Meghan.Kincaid@YATESCOUNTYNY.GOV>
Sent: Friday, October 31, 2025 11:53 AM
To: RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US <RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US>
Subject: [External] merging parcels
STOP | THINK | ACT
External email detected. Do not click on links or open attachments from unknown sources. Be alert for phishing attempts & report suspicious email IT Security.
Good morning -
I have a follow-up question related to a question I had asked previously.
The backstory - A property owner had requested via a parcel combo form for my tax mapper to combine two adjacent parcels, and she denied it twice because the ownership was not the same.
On parcel A - The son is the sole owner. On parcel B - The son is the owner and the mother has Life Use.
Now the son filed a deed stating that the intention of the deed is to merge the two parcels.
So, my previous question was - Would you merge them? The lawyer is pushing the issue looking for tax law for why we can't.
At the time of my question, one of you (thank you) sent me this Op of Counsel
Volume 5 - Opinions of Counsel SBEA
No. 118
How I read that is that the assessor could make the determination whether to allow the parcels to be merged on the role, though this would be for assisting with assessing and tax bill purposes, and NOT in
determination of legal ownership. Ok... fine with that.
Now the lawyer states that the intention is also for the mother's Life Use to carry to the newly MERGED parcel, even though it states nothing about her extending Life Use in the deed to the newly merged
parcel. In fact, she is not mentioned in the deed and did not sign it.
On top of that, the parcel with the house is NOT currently the one the mother has Life Use on. Instead, the son lives there and has a Basic STAR on it. (The other parcel is a vacant lot.)
Would you put the Life Use on the new parcel? The only thing that the new deed states is that the FATHER's Life Use was extinguished because he passed away, but nothing about the mother's life use.
Even if it was put on, and if the mother is living there, too - and if she applied for an Enhanced STAR, it would have to be a credit, not an exemption. What a cluster.
I would appreciated any thoughts. This lawyer is being... persistent.
Thank you and Happy Halloween!!!
~ Meghan.

On Thu, Mar 12, 2026, 4:50 PM Corey Metz <00000106db98a9de-dmarc-request@list-nysac.us> wrote:
Just as an FYI for towns, the town has to pass a local law to allow demolition costs to be added as a charge on the tax bill. Lawn mowing/cleanup costs do not need a local law. We require a
cover sheet for reporting all re-levies to us which I highly recommend because otherwise they can send you a bunch of random bills and will say "relevy these please!" without even a hint of what the total is supposed to be.
Corey Metz
(She/her/hers)

Good morning everyone,
Last year, the Jefferson County Legislature passed a new resolution concerning cleanup/demolition of dangerous properties.  I reached out to Candy and she graciously passed on Lewis County's process for handling the relevy of the costs
involved if the property owner doesn't pay them when billed.  Thank you very much Candy!
I passed on Lewis County's method to other department heads in our County who will work on parts of the process and they asked me to check with more Counties to see if they may have a similar or different process.  Specifically, they would
like to know if we are able to add the relevy directly to the Town & County bill in January as a special charge.
However, any ideas/suggestions on the subject would be appreciated!

To: RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US
Subject: merging parcels
Caution: This is an external email. Please take care when clicking links or opening attachments. When in doubt, contact the Help Desk.
Good morning -
I have a follow-up question related to a question I had asked previously.
The backstory - A property owner had requested via a parcel combo form for my tax mapper to combine two adjacent parcels, and she denied it twice because the ownership was not the same.
On parcel A - The son is the sole owner. On parcel B - The son is the owner and the mother has Life Use.
Now the son filed a deed stating that the intention of the deed is to merge the two parcels.
So, my previous question was - Would you merge them? The lawyer is pushing the issue looking for tax law for why we can't.
At the time of my question, one of you (thank you) sent me this Op of Counsel
Volume 5 - Opinions of Counsel SBEA No. 118
How I read that is that the assessor could make the determination whether to allow the parcels to be merged on the role, though this would be for assisting with assessing and tax bill purposes, and NOT in
determination of legal ownership. Ok... fine with that.
Now the lawyer states that the intention is also for the mother's Life Use to carry to the newly MERGED parcel, even though it states nothing about her extending Life Use in the deed to the newly merged parcel.
In fact, she is not mentioned in the deed and did not sign it.
On top of that, the parcel with the house is NOT currently the one the mother has Life Use on. Instead, the son lives there and has a Basic STAR on it. (The other parcel is a vacant lot.)
Would you put the Life Use on the new parcel? The only thing that the new deed states is that the FATHER's Life Use was extinguished because he passed away, but nothing about the mother's life use.
Even if it was put on, and if the mother is living there, too - and if she applied for an Enhanced STAR, it would have to be a credit, not an exemption. What a cluster.
I would appreciated any thoughts. This lawyer is being... persistent.
Thank you and Happy Halloween!!!
~ Meghan.

Subject: Conference Follow up
Hello,
Happy First day of the Spring of Deception, or Third Winter...hard to know where we're at!
Wanted to follow up with everyone after the Conference of Awkwardness, well for me anyway, and I assume for my fellow "early adopters". If you read, Crossing the Chasm (highly recommended),
it examines the dynamics faced by innovative tech products.  The theory is there is a chasm between early adopters of new tech and the pragmatists who are generally the early majority. Primarily a sales and marketing book, it explores differing expectations
and has some relevance to the PSO roll out.
Anyway, mostly I want to provide an update on the NDA issue. I have asked for and received some clarification. I do have the latitude to discuss operational functionality of my
county's RPSO currently in production. However, I need to be mindful of any ongoing discussions and development scenarios originating from the constituent's group, or any observations, process suggestions and enhancements, or wish list items that may be on
the drawing board but are not currently in the production environment.
It would have been valuable to have this information a couple of days ago. Armed with that, I certainly would have spent more time in the networking suite!
There were struggles with our early adoption. And yes, our T&C tax cycle was difficult. We had issues to overcome...one battle after another! Yes, we were late and yes, the phones
were busy, but genuine typical complete bills and rolls went out. Sometimes you just don't know there is an issue until you get to that point. I give tremendous credit to my staff, our town clerks and collectors, our Treasurer's Office, and especially the
RPSO team for their effort and dedication to seeing it through. I hope the product benefitted from our pain.
Each county is different. We have our own unique set of challenges and operational structures. I will say I encourage every county in a position to do so to sign on. With each addition
and with each new obstacle overcome the system improves. There really isn't another alternative, for us at least. V4 is literally a dead language. Your next hardware upgrade could render it incompatible and good luck finding someone to bang out a patch with
a script to fix it.
Feel free to reach out, I'll respond if I am able.
Sláinte
Barry
Barry L. Baker, CCD
Hamilton County Real Property Tax Services
102 County View Drive
Lake Pleasant, NY 12108
518-548-5531
realproperty@hamiltoncountyny.gov
https://www.hamiltoncounty.com

subject: Re: [EXTERNAL] Conference Follow up
body:
Thanks, Barry. I realize that the NDA made it difficult for you to interact with us and therefore understandably awkward. I am probably not alone in wondering why the state is insisting on so much secrecy, particularly since they are a
public entity and not some software start-up in Silicon Valley hoping for a splashy debut so they can get bought up by some larger tech company. We are their intended users, after all, and the way that this has been presented to us is has been... well, odd.
My main concern now has more to do with ORPS expecting my county to do the conversion and training in the month or so before Taxable Status Date. But not just my county; I imagine there will not be too many assessors around the state that
would be willing to have to learn and use a new system for most of their work during that time. It comes across as thoughtless and uncaring.

subject: Approval Routing Sheet
body:
Hello,
For corrections that are $2,500 and below, we have a resolution designating our County Auditor as the person authorized to sign off.  After I sign and approve,
we route to our Commissioner of Finance, then it formerly went to the County Attorney's office for signature, then to the County Exec, the Auditor, and then back to the COF for payment.  Finally, a copy comes back to me.
I am trying to eliminate the County Attorney for these smaller ones.  Can I get an idea on how you all route your smaller corrections?  Is procedure typically
for all corrections to funnel through the County Attorney?  Just the ones above $2,500--or none?
Thanks, Trish
Trish McLoughlin
Director  ● Office of Real Property Tax Services

subject: merging parcels
body:
Good morning -
I have a follow-up question related to a question I had asked previously.
The backstory - A property owner had requested via a parcel combo form for my tax mapper to combine two adjacent parcels, and she denied it twice because the ownership was not the same.
On parcel A - The son is the sole owner. On parcel B - The son is the owner and the mother has Life Use.
Now the son filed a deed stating that the intention of the deed is to merge the two parcels.
So, my previous question was - Would you merge them? The lawyer is pushing the issue looking for tax law for why we can't.
At the time of my question, one of you (thank you) sent me this Op of Counsel
Volume 5 - Opinions of Counsel SBEA No. 118
How I read that is that the assessor could make the determination whether to allow the parcels to be merged on the role, though this would be for assisting with assessing and tax bill purposes, and NOT in
determination of legal ownership. Ok... fine with that.
Now the lawyer states that the intention is also for the mother's Life Use to carry to the newly MERGED parcel, even though it states nothing about her extending Life Use in the deed to the newly merged parcel.
In fact, she is not mentioned in the deed and did not sign it.
On top of that, the parcel with the house is NOT currently the one the mother has Life Use on. Instead, the son lives there and has a Basic STAR on it. (The other parcel is a vacant lot.)
Would you put the Life Use on the new parcel? The only thing that the new deed states is that the FATHER's Life Use was extinguished because he passed away, but nothing about the mother's life use.
Even if it was put on, and if the mother is living there, too - and if she applied for an Enhanced STAR, it would have to be a credit, not an exemption. What a cluster.
I would appreciated any thoughts. This lawyer is being... persistent.
Thank you and Happy Halloween!!!
~ Meghan.
Meghan K. Kincaid
Director for Real Property Tax Services
Yates County

Penn Yan, NY  14527

subject: inventory
body:
Good morning everyone,
Need some feedback on this one...
A property is situated across town lines.... although the house is assessed in one town - it is clearly in the adjoining town  - both visually with the aerial photography and the survey map we have of the property.
The assessor for the town where the house is assessed is fine with the adjoining town taking the inventory however the other assessor is adamant that state law prohibits this !
No response from him when I asked for the state law -
Last year this same situation happened within two other munis and the assessors willingly updated the inventory...
Thoughts????
Anna

subject: Script for income check of SR Citizen Exemption
body:
Hi everyone,
At the conference in Latham last week, there was a request for a way to verify the incomes entered in the columns for 4180 exemptions. The goal is to ensure that the values match
appropriately and comply with any applicable laws your county may have in place.
To assist with this, below is a script that can be run in Open Interactive SQL that our CRM helped us create. This script will generate a listing of all senior citizen exemptions
along with their corresponding incomes for each category: County, Town, School, and Village.
You can also export the resulting listing to a CSV file and open it in Excel, which makes it easier to sort, filter, and identify any anomalies.
Hope this helps.
Thank you
Tammy Lacey, CCD

subject: Grievance Day - By Appointment Only?
body:
Hello everyone,
I have an assessor that has scheduled normal grievance day from 4pm to 6pm and then 6pm to 8pm by appointment only.  Is this something you've seen before?
What if someone doesn't send their RP-524 form in ahead of time or make an appointment and just shows up to the hearing but no one is there because there were not appointments after 6pm?  How does that work?
Does the town have to adopt a resolution or LL?  What section of law allows this?
Candy Akin, CCD
Real Property Tax Director
2025-2026 President, NYSACDRPTS
O: 315-376-5336
M: 315-907-2032
candyakin@lewiscounty.ny.gov
7660 North State St. | Lowville, NY 13367

subject: Re: Grievance Day - By Appointment Only?
body:
I have multiple assessors that do "by appointment" for grievance day when they are expecting a huge influx of people. I would not say that negates the fact that they should still be there for the entire 4 hours. Someone still has the right to show up at 7:45
to turn in a Grievance Application. The assessor could schedule an adjourned hearing, but they still need to be there to accept the application.
Hannah Carson, Director
Essex County Real Property Tax Services
7551 Court St, PO Box
217
Elizabethtown NY 12932
(518) 873-3395

subject: Village Billing
body:
Hello,
I have asked this question before, and came to the conclusion that we would use our C/T databases (we have standalones) with the prior roll year for Village
bill processing.  I have a few village clerks telling me that they often have billing address updates/sales between C/T and Village billing.  If I were to use the Tentative Roll databases that my assessors bring me in mid-April for Village billing (and prior
roll year), so that I have the most up to date owners and addresses, is there any disadvantage to this?  I feel like there was a reason or a hiccup I had using the Tentative Roll database, and I can't remember what it was.
Thanks for your thoughts.  Trish
Trish McLoughlin

subject: 485-b Question
body:
Someone asked for the County's resolution for our 485-b exemption and in digging around I have found a couple of resolutions from the 1970s but nothing more recent. The most recent one from 1979 seems to be adopting a special 485 exemption
for "eligible business facilities" that meet certain criteria, but we just found that one and I do not know of any property that has received that. We have been applying a basic, ten year 485-b exemption for decades around here. The property owner has to apply
for it, and the exemption starts at 50%, goes down 5% per year for ten years. Improvement value has to be $10,000 or higher, with no maximum amount.
My question for you: do we need a local law or resolution for the basic 485-b, or is that an exemption that applies unless you opt out? I would not like to find out that we have been doing something wrong for the past 25 or 30 years...
Paul Wiley
Director
Orange County Office of Real Property
255 Main St
Goshen, NY 10924
O: (845) 291-2494
C: (845) 806-0817

body:
You can never really opt out 485-b.  However, you can reduce the percentage off that you offer to 0% - which effectively opts you out of the exemption.
So if you didn't do anything, you offer the 50% exemption in year 1.

Thanks, Barry. I realize that the NDA made it difficult for you to interact with us and therefore understandably awkward. I am probably not alone in wondering why the state is insisting on so much secrecy, particularly since they are a
public entity and not some software start-up in Silicon Valley hoping for a splashy debut so they can get bought up by some larger tech company. We are their intended users, after all, and the way that this has been presented to us is has been... well, odd.
My main concern now has more to do with ORPS expecting my county to do the conversion and training in the month or so before Taxable Status Date. But not just my county; I imagine there will not be too many assessors around the state that
would be willing to have to learn and use a new system for most of their work during that time. It comes across as thoughtless and uncaring.
Paul Wiley
Director
Orange County Office of Real Property
255 Main St
Goshen, NY 10924
O: (845) 291-2494
C: (845) 806-0817
From: Real Property Tax Directors <RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US>
On Behalf Of Barry Baker
Sent: Friday, March 20, 2026 2:12 PM
To: RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US
Subject: [EXTERNAL] Conference Follow up
Hello,
Happy First day of the Spring of Deception, or Third Winter...hard to know where we're at!
Wanted to follow up with everyone after the Conference of Awkwardness, well for me anyway, and I assume for my fellow "early adopters". If you read, Crossing the Chasm (highly recommended),
it examines the dynamics faced by innovative tech products.  The theory is there is a chasm between early adopters of new tech and the pragmatists who are generally the early majority. Primarily a sales and marketing book, it explores differing expectations
and has some relevance to the PSO roll out.
Anyway, mostly I want to provide an update on the NDA issue. I have asked for and received some clarification. I do have the latitude to discuss operational functionality of my
county's RPSO currently in production. However, I need to be mindful of any ongoing discussions and development scenarios originating from the constituent's group, or any observations, process suggestions and enhancements, or wish list items that may be on
the drawing board but are not currently in the production environment.
It would have been valuable to have this information a couple of days ago. Armed with that, I certainly would have spent more time in the networking suite!
There were struggles with our early adoption. And yes, our T&C tax cycle was difficult. We had issues to overcome...one battle after another! Yes, we were late and yes, the phones
were busy, but genuine typical complete bills and rolls went out. Sometimes you just don't know there is an issue until you get to that point. I give tremendous credit to my staff, our town clerks and collectors, our Treasurer's Office, and especially the
RPSO team for their effort and dedication to seeing it through. I hope the product benefitted from our pain.
Each county is different. We have our own unique set of challenges and operational structures. I will say I encourage every county in a position to do so to sign on. With each addition
and with each new obstacle overcome the system improves. There really isn't another alternative, for us at least. V4 is literally a dead language. Your next hardware upgrade could render it incompatible and good luck finding someone to bang out a patch with
a script to fix it.
Feel free to reach out, I'll respond if I am able.
Sláinte
Barry
Barry L. Baker, CCD
Hamilton County Real Property Tax Services
102 County View Drive
Lake Pleasant, NY 12108
518-548-5531
realproperty@hamiltoncountyny.gov
https://www.hamiltoncounty.com

subject: Changing Special District Units for Villages
body:
Question:
Can a village change how their special district units are calculated after final roll but before their bills? I have a village that wants to change from 1 unit per parcel, to adding units for 2/3 family homes. In terms of changing the units themselves, I am
sure that's fine (we do it for our sewer units after the final roll is done) but that's not "we're changing how they're calculated." And I keep getting pulled away from Opinions of Counsel to find the answer myself, so...help? And would such changes require
a COE?

Thanks, Barry. I realize that the NDA made it difficult for you to interact with us and therefore understandably awkward. I am probably not alone in wondering why the state is insisting on so much secrecy, particularly since they are a
public entity and not some software start-up in Silicon Valley hoping for a splashy debut so they can get bought up by some larger tech company. We are their intended users, after all, and the way that this has been presented to us is has been... well, odd.
My main concern now has more to do with ORPS expecting my county to do the conversion and training in the month or so before Taxable Status Date. But not just my county; I imagine there will not be too many assessors around the state that
would be willing to have to learn and use a new system for most of their work during that time. It comes across as thoughtless and uncaring.

On Behalf Of Barry Baker
Sent: Friday, March 20, 2026 2:12 PM
To: RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US
Subject: [EXTERNAL] Conference Follow up
Hello,
Happy First day of the Spring of Deception, or Third Winter...hard to know where we're at!
Wanted to follow up with everyone after the Conference of Awkwardness, well for me anyway, and I assume for my fellow "early adopters". If you read, Crossing the Chasm (highly recommended),
it examines the dynamics faced by innovative tech products.  The theory is there is a chasm between early adopters of new tech and the pragmatists who are generally the early majority. Primarily a sales and marketing book, it explores differing expectations
and has some relevance to the PSO roll out.
Anyway, mostly I want to provide an update on the NDA issue. I have asked for and received some clarification. I do have the latitude to discuss operational functionality of my
county's RPSO currently in production. However, I need to be mindful of any ongoing discussions and development scenarios originating from the constituent's group, or any observations, process suggestions and enhancements, or wish list items that may be on
the drawing board but are not currently in the production environment.
It would have been valuable to have this information a couple of days ago. Armed with that, I certainly would have spent more time in the networking suite!
There were struggles with our early adoption. And yes, our T&C tax cycle was difficult. We had issues to overcome...one battle after another! Yes, we were late and yes, the phones
were busy, but genuine typical complete bills and rolls went out. Sometimes you just don't know there is an issue until you get to that point. I give tremendous credit to my staff, our town clerks and collectors, our Treasurer's Office, and especially the
RPSO team for their effort and dedication to seeing it through. I hope the product benefitted from our pain.
Each county is different. We have our own unique set of challenges and operational structures. I will say I encourage every county in a position to do so to sign on. With each addition
and with each new obstacle overcome the system improves. There really isn't another alternative, for us at least. V4 is literally a dead language. Your next hardware upgrade could render it incompatible and good luck finding someone to bang out a patch with
a script to fix it.
Feel free to reach out, I'll respond if I am able.
Sláinte
Barry
Barry L. Baker, CCD
Hamilton County Real Property Tax Services
102 County View Drive
Lake Pleasant, NY 12108
518-548-5531
realproperty@hamiltoncountyny.gov
https://www.hamiltoncounty.com

Has anyone that is currently using Beacon heard how the new RPSO program will work out with extracting the data?  I have agreed to
be one of the first in the Central Region to convert to RPSO and the reply I got when I asked the State was:
Here's the response from the RPSO team,
When you say
"pull data directly from RPSv4 on a daily basis" I'm interpreting that to mean getting data directly from tables on the live RPSV4 database.  If that is your current set-up then that would have to change
a little in RPSO.  Going forward, municipalities would not be allowed to connect to the live data outside of RPSO.  RPSO/ORPTS are aware that many municipalities throughout the state have agreements with SDG/Beacon and others to update municipal web pages.
RPSO would produce an extract of data and SDG/Beacon would get the data from that extract.  ORPTS will work with you to meet your needs by providing regular data extracts

subject: Re: Thoughts on Beacon?
body:
Has anyone that is currently using Beacon heard how the new RPSO program will work out with extracting the data?  I have agreed to
be one of the first in the Central Region to convert to RPSO and the reply I got when I asked the State was:
Here's the response from the RPSO team,
When you say "pull data directly from RPSv4 on a daily basis" I'm interpreting that to mean getting data directly from tables on the live RPSV4 database.  If that is your current set-up then that would have
to change a little in RPSO.  Going forward, municipalities would not be allowed to connect to the live data outside of RPSO.  RPSO/ORPTS are aware that many municipalities throughout the state have agreements with SDG/Beacon and others to update municipal
web pages.  RPSO would produce an extract of data and SDG/Beacon would get the data from that extract.  ORPTS will work with you to meet your needs by providing regular data extracts
Laura Fox, Director
Cortland County Real Property Tax Services
607-753-5142

Thanks, Barry. I realize that the NDA made it difficult for you to interact with us and therefore understandably awkward. I am probably not alone in wondering why the state is insisting on so much secrecy, particularly since they are a
public entity and not some software start-up in Silicon Valley hoping for a splashy debut so they can get bought up by some larger tech company. We are their intended users, after all, and the way that this has been presented to us is has been... well, odd.
My main concern now has more to do with ORPS expecting my county to do the conversion and training in the month or so before Taxable Status Date. But not just my county; I imagine there will not be too many assessors around the state that
would be willing to have to learn and use a new system for most of their work during that time. It comes across as thoughtless and uncaring.
Paul Wiley
Director
Orange County Office of Real Property
255 Main St
Goshen, NY 10924
O: (845) 291-2494
C: (845) 806-0817
From: Real Property Tax Directors <RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US>
On Behalf Of Barry Baker
Sent: Friday, March 20, 2026 2:12 PM
To: RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US
Subject: [EXTERNAL] Conference Follow up
Hello,
Happy First day of the Spring of Deception, or Third Winter...hard to know where we're at!
Wanted to follow up with everyone after the Conference of Awkwardness, well for me anyway, and I assume for my fellow "early adopters". If you read, Crossing the Chasm (highly recommended),
it examines the dynamics faced by innovative tech products.  The theory is there is a chasm between early adopters of new tech and the pragmatists who are generally the early majority. Primarily a sales and marketing book, it explores differing expectations
and has some relevance to the PSO roll out.
Anyway, mostly I want to provide an update on the NDA issue. I have asked for and received some clarification. I do have the latitude to discuss operational functionality of my
county's RPSO currently in production. However, I need to be mindful of any ongoing discussions and development scenarios originating from the constituent's group, or any observations, process suggestions and enhancements, or wish list items that may be on
the drawing board but are not currently in the production environment.
It would have been valuable to have this information a couple of days ago. Armed with that, I certainly would have spent more time in the networking suite!
There were struggles with our early adoption. And yes, our T&C tax cycle was difficult. We had issues to overcome...one battle after another! Yes, we were late and yes, the phones
were busy, but genuine typical complete bills and rolls went out. Sometimes you just don't know there is an issue until you get to that point. I give tremendous credit to my staff, our town clerks and collectors, our Treasurer's Office, and especially the
RPSO team for their effort and dedication to seeing it through. I hope the product benefitted from our pain.
Each county is different. We have our own unique set of challenges and operational structures. I will say I encourage every county in a position to do so to sign on. With each addition
and with each new obstacle overcome the system improves. There really isn't another alternative, for us at least. V4 is literally a dead language. Your next hardware upgrade could render it incompatible and good luck finding someone to bang out a patch with
a script to fix it.
Feel free to reach out, I'll respond if I am able.
Sláinte
Barry
Barry L. Baker, CCD
Hamilton County Real Property Tax Services
102 County View Drive
Lake Pleasant, NY 12108
518-548-5531
realproperty@hamiltoncountyny.gov
https://www.hamiltoncounty.com

subject: Income Verification for Seniors
body:
Hello,
I have an assessor who abruptly left their position, and we now have someone who is very capable as a replacement.  It is looking like not much income verification
was being done previously for the Senior exemption, and the new person is requiring the income verification.  I had a homeowner just call me complaining that the new assessor asked for a copy of the Trust to see how she benefits, also a Schedule 1, and then
she gave the front page of her tax return that has her income info on it.  Assessor now is saying he needs the entire tax return, in this person's words, 'in case we get audited'.  This homeowner feels that this is an invasion of her privacy--that she has given
him enough.  She wants to know if this is typical to ask for the full tax return.  I told her I would reach out to my group.
Thanks, T
Trish McLoughlin
Director  ● Office of Real Property Tax Services
PHONE | 845.808.1000 ● X-49315 | WEBSITE |
PUTNAMCOUNTYNY.COM
PUTNAM COUNTY GOVERNMENT NEW YORK
"Empowering Putnam County through dedicated service."

subject: Ownership Correction Question – Conflicting Deeds / Easement vs. Fee
body:
Hi everyone,
I'm looking for some guidance on a parcel with a conflicting chain of title and how others would handle it. I have a piece of land where there is a recorded deed that appears to establish fee ownership to one party. However, there is also a subsequent recorded
deed where a different grantor conveyed the parcel as if they held fee title, when, based on prior records, it appears they only held an easement interest at the time. So essentially, the parcel was later conveyed as fee when it likely should have only involved
an easement.
Could we just update the ownership on the roll based on the deed that appears to correctly establish fee ownership, even though there is a later recorded deed that seems to have incorrectly conveyed the parcel? Or would you require a corrective deed (or
other recorded instrument) before making any ownership change?
Thank you in advance for your help!
Victoria Blancato
Director, Real Property Tax Services
Wyoming County
143 North Main Street, Warsaw, NY 14569
Phone: (585) 786-8828 | Email: vblancato@wyomingcountyny.gov
https://www.wyomingcountyny.gov/

subject: Beacon Users - Property Address Question
body:
Hello,
I just noticed in Beacon that the property address on a parcel was not stated correctly in the Property Data/Property Address section.  It was putting the
Town that the property is in, instead of the actual parcel mailing address, which can often times be different from the name of the town.  It did have the correct zip code, though.  Then we found parcels in Beacon that had no zip code in the Property Address.
The assessor and I figured out that Beacon is pulling from the Parcel tab in RPS under Property Location.  This particular assessor's Parcel Tab has the name
of the Town put in the Town/City entry, not the actual postal address, and then has the correct zip code, so often times, in his case, the 'Town' is not in harmony with the zip code (which coincides with the actual mailing/postal address of the parcel).  This
page was set up from years past, not him.
So, now I'm not happy with how Beacon is displaying my Property Addresses.  I'm having thoughts of maybe getting a script from ORPTS to have T/Kent put into
his Town/City spot in Property Location, and then NO zip code, so that Beacon will pull the street, then put T/Kent, and that's it.  Even though up top it already shows the municipality, and I was hoping to have a legal property address for public or mailing
purposes in this location, I don't think there is an easy way to do this, if the Property Location of the Parcel Tab was not maintained that way.  We pulled up a few other towns, and the problem seems to be the same throughout my towns.  One example is he
has a parcel that has a street address of Hortontown Rd which is in the T/Kent, but Hopewell Jct postal address--and yet his Parcel Location tab in RPS apparently has Kent in the town/city, and then has a zip code of Carmel for some reason!  A mess.  If the
owner did not live at the parcel location (which had the full, correct mailing address of this property), and had a Florida mailing address under Owner, then one would have no idea where this parcel was, except that it is in the T/Kent.
Sorry, very long winded.  Do you Beacon users have your Parcel Tab/Property Location addresses in RPS filled out completely with correct mailing addresses
for the parcel?  I think mine are so messed up, that I may need to just have a script done for my towns' RPS databases to make the city/town on the Parcel tab/Property Location just say T/_____  or V/_____ , with NO zip codes, and settle for not having
a parcel full legal address on Beacon.
I've attached a Beacon screenshot of a parcel that is located in the Town of Patterson.  At the top, it has OWNER, and the address of the parcel, as they live
there.  See below in Property Data/Property Address, it has the Town, and the zip code that matches that town--which is technically wrong.  The property address should say Brewster, NY 10509.  But this is the way that it has been put into the Parcel Tab/Property
Location of RPS from many years ago.  I either want it legally correct, or to just have the Town stated here with no zip code.
Thoughts from Beacon users?  Anyone with this issue?  Please don't tell me that all of your RPS Parcel Tab/Property Locations all have the correct legal mailing
addresses of the parcel ☹ and Beacon is populating perfectly!
Thanks, Trish
Trish McLoughlin
Director  ● Office of Real Property Tax Services

PUTNAMCOUNTYNY.COM
PUTNAM COUNTY GOVERNMENT NEW YORK

I already know what I am going to say is ridiculous, but it is the opinion of ORPTS and the RPSO team...
The City/Town field is not for mailing purposes.  The City/Town is supposed to be the actual city/town that the parcel is located in.  For example, if a parcel is in the Town of East Fishkill
but the mailing address for that parcel is Hopewell Junction, the City/Town field on the parcel screen is supposed to say East Fishkill.
I tried to argue this with the RPSO team that it made no sense, but I did not win that fight, (I did win others).  They could not understand why someone would want to mail something to the parcel
and not the owner's mailing address.  They did add a new field in RPSO called Hamlet where I guess you can put the mailing city/town into.
Either way, the city/town and zip fields are not maintained in Dutchess and are not displayed on our parcel viewer site.

subject: RPS's Parcel Tab - Parcel Location
body:
Hello,
Just looking to see if I am asking for something that is unreasonable in RPSO.
I am being told that in the above section of RPS, in the City/Town space, ORPTS expects that the assessors are inputting the municipality.  Some of my towns
are doing this.  However, they are then putting in the zip code that matches the legal mailing address of the parcel--which if put together as an address--it doesn't work on many.  My town of Kent is not a postal address.  This is where my 3rd party,
Beacon, pulls from, for the Parcel/Property Address.  It turns into a wonky address.
I ask you.  Wouldn't it be useful for the property's legal MAILING address be located here in the Parcel tab, Parcel Location?  The SWIS and Municipality is
already located at the top of the screen.  I believe the legal mailing address of the parcel would be useful for a printout of a mailing list of all properties within a school district or town/city/village, if a mailing is desired for all RESIDENTS of the
parcel address, NOT necessarily owners.  If this parcel page is being filled out with the municipality in this location, and in some of my towns, no zip code at all, then is there any place in RPS that would allow for a custom report to generate a mailing
list for all PARCEL locations?  ORPTS may not deem this useful, but I think it would be.  I just had a school district ask for a mailing list for all residential (200-299) parcels in their school district--to reach the household resident (which often times
is not the owner.   I could see from the list that populated, the addresses were not making sense--and this is how I found the issue.  I guess the custom report pulls from this page?  I was asking for property address, NOT owner address.
Am I wrong, is there another location in RPS that has the legal mailing address of the parcel?  Do most of you just put in the municipality for the City/Town
on the Parcel page, or do you put in the legal mailing address of the parcel here?
Thanks, Trish
Trish McLoughlin
Director  ● Office of Real Property Tax Services
PHONE | 845.808.1000 ● X-49315 | WEBSITE |
PUTNAMCOUNTYNY.COM
PUTNAM COUNTY GOVERNMENT NEW YORK
"Empowering Putnam County through dedicated service."

subject: Re: EXTERNAL RPS's Parcel Tab - Parcel Location
body:
Parcel folder is for data specific to that specific parcel and remains consistent throughout the lifetime of that parcel, excepting mapping changes
and updates.  As the owner is variable data related to the current owner, including mailing address, it is not stored in the parcel folder.  It is found in the owner folder.  The data in the Parcel folder was never intended to be used for mailing addresses
or owner related information.  As noted there is some confusion about this distinction among RPS V4 users.
If your towns have erroneous data in the Parcel folder it is possible to batch in the correct data.  That would be the most efficient way to correct
the errors.  RPS V4 was not built to provide mailing addresses for all residents or units within a parcel.  It does not capture that level of data and was not intended to.
I create an annual mailing list report for my entire county.  Based on data limitations this list only on contains mailing addresses for the owners
- not all property residents.  Our PR folks are working to send out a mailer to all residents within the county.  They contacted a local mail house to use their mass distribution list for this purpose.
Using Custom Reports - Assessment Group you can create a report with mailing lists for just the 200s in a given school district.
Michael McGuire, IAO, CCD
Director

112 State Street, Room 1103, Albany, NY 12207

subject: Re: RPS's Parcel Tab - Parcel Location
body:
Some people who received this message don't often get email from 00000120eeb6c274-dmarc-request@list-nysac.us.
Learn why this is important
The problem being this creates an issue for the physical location address for 911 / EMS response, etc.
We have several towns where the Parcel Location Address is impacted by what post office the property is serviced by. And in many cases, they are not even in the same county. This does create issues for delivery service and for collection of occupancy and sales
taxes.
What we do is put the Street and City/Town only in Parcel Location and leave the zip code blank. The mailing address is generated from the Owner Field for tax bills an other purposes.
Best,

Subject:        Ownership Correction Question - Conflicting Deeds / Easement vs. Fee
Sent by:        "Real Property Tax Directors" <RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US>
Hi everyone,
I'm looking for some guidance on a parcel with a conflicting chain of title and how others would handle it. I have a piece of land where there is a recorded deed that appears to establish fee ownership to one party. However, there
is also a subsequent recorded deed where a different grantor conveyed the parcel as if they held fee title, when, based on prior records, it appears they only held an easement interest at the time. So essentially, the parcel was later conveyed as fee when
it likely should have only involved an easement.
Could we just update the ownership on the roll based on the deed that appears to correctly establish fee ownership, even though there is a later recorded deed that seems to have incorrectly conveyed the parcel? Or would you require
a corrective deed (or other recorded instrument) before making any ownership change?
Thank you in advance for your help!

subject: SOLAR-Wind Class
body:
Good Afternoon:
Who would be interested in taking a solar/wind class? IDA vs. private exemptions. Solar model ( which holy heck who does these things)??!! I know that in Franklin County we have seen an influx of solar projects over the last 2 years and have many new ones
coming in the future. I am currently learning more about KWdc and KW ac watts than I ever wanted to know, NYSERDA, and appraisals that come with these applications that are 3,000 pages long and things that you need are tucked in there..somewhere?? 🤐😏
I would love someone who is an expert in this to help guide us through this crazy process. I have created an Excel document to calculate the private solar exemption -49500 and where to find that information in the appraisal ( again they are not great about
giving it to you in a gift package).
Oh and if anyone else is wondering why these are currently springing up like tulips, it is because in order to receive the 15 year exemption, they must apply by 1/1/2030, which means all of this will be sitting here lifeless by 2045.. The average lifespan
according to the appraisal is  only 35 years.
Ok I am off my soapbox... please let me know if anyone else is interested as much as me. Hopefully we can find someone who knows NYSERDA, the "model", etc...

subject: property owned by another muni
body:
Good afternoon -
One of my assessors just called me. She just received an email from an attorney for a town outside of our county. That town recently acquired a parcel in our county, and he was emailing to "double-check that
the parcel would be wholly exempt since it is owned by the town." He said that the town is planning to use the parcel for conservation.
What is the property procedure for this to be a Roll Section 8 parcel?
I advised my assessor to reach out to her attorney. However, my feeling is that they would have had to request the parcel to be exempt by 3/1. They also would have to meet one of the specific conservation
mentioned in RPTL 406(2) - (Flood control and soil conservation projects include: construction of dikes, drains, check-dams, pipes, and new or altered channels; reforestation or the planting
of shrubs and plants; and any other improvements necessary for soil erosion control or watershed protection.), not just be
planning to use it for conservation.
Furthermore, from what I am reading, each of the taxing jurisdictions (town, county, school district) would each have had to pass a resolution for it to be exempt, as well. Am
I correct on that?
Any guidance would be appreciated!!
Thank you,
Meghan.

subject: Late City Budget
body:
This is a first for me. I have a city that has a May 1st warrant date. It appears that they will not pass a budget by then. We just process their file and they print their own bills. I can't think of anything that will happen
other than their bills going out late. Anything I'm missing with this? There's got to be someone out here that has had to deal with something similar and can fill me in.
Thanks

subject: totals don't match
body:
Okee... So, here is a weird one. For one of my towns, when I run the Tentative Roll, it is dropping a parcel.
The Roll Section Town Summary is showing one more parcel and an assessed value of $1,300,000 more than the Tentative Roll is showing.
The assessor's file matches my Roll Section Summary. Yet, whatever other report I run to try to find the parcel, it is not showing a parcel valued at $1,300,000. All custom reports show the number of parcel as one less than the Roll Section
Summary.
Even when I hit Search in RPS, without giving it any additional criteria, and then have it list in order of assessed value, it is not showing a parcel at that value. Taxable values are showing $1,300,000 off, as well.
I had one time in the past where an assessor put alpha characters in the UCAR number for a new utility, and only some reports were reading the parcel, but this is a regular Roll Section 1 parcel.
Has anyone ever run into this? Help!!
Thanks for any suggestions,
Meghan.
Meghan K. Kincaid

body:
State Pauses Rollout of RPS Online
Folks,
In case you are not a NYSAA member I wanted to share this statement.
To add to this - yesterday the RPSO Constituents Group met with ORPTS.  At that meeting ORPTS announced the pause.  They will be conducting more extensive in house testing
before resuming conversions.  Their intended plan is to complete a typical year's assessment calendar in house within RPSO to identify issues, bugs, etc.  This is why I requested annual calendars yesterday.  The more data we can provide about our annual cycles
the more dynamic and robust the testing.
Once the internal testing is complete the RPSO Constituents Group will conduct additional testing.
Obviously this is a less than ideal situation and I am sure most you, like me, are wondering what they did test in house...
While this is a delay and setback it does provide an opportunity for improvement.
Thanks,
Michael McGuire, IAO, CCD

State Pauses Rollout of RPS Online
Dear Members,
I would like to provide an update regarding the State's Real Property Valuation System (RPS Online).
At NYSAA's most recent Executive Board meeting, a committee was formed to investigate concerns that had been raised regarding the functionality of the new system being implemented
by the New York State Office of Real Property Tax Services (ORPTS).
Following that decision, at the recent Real Property Tax Committee (RPTAC) meeting, we formally requested that the State provide our committee with access to the RPS Online testing
environment. The goal was to allow for a thorough, hands-on review so that we could better assess the validity of the issues being reported and provide meaningful, experience-based feedback.
Since that time, the State has announced that it is pausing the rollout of RPS Online.
We appreciate the State's willingness to recognize the importance of addressing these concerns and the value of stakeholder input in this process. We believe this pause provides an
opportunity to ensure that the system ultimately meets the needs of the assessing community.
We look forward to continuing to work collaboratively with New York State Department of Taxation and Finance and ORPTS to support the development and successful implementation of a
strong and effective RPS Online system.
Thank you for your continued engagement and support.
Warren J Wheeler, IAO
Executive Director, NYSAA

subject: Re: EXTERNAL Disabled Vets Exemption
body:
Folks,
A little context that I found helpful with the veterans exemption.  There are many other states that offer a 100% exemption for disabled veterans.  There is a national push
for this type of tax exemption, what we are experiencing is that push.
Larry provided the Assembly text, there is always proposed text in the Senate one house budget that greatly expands the pool of eligible applicants.  I attached the proposed
text, Part NN.
Candy and I met with Patrick Cummings from NYSAC, Governors Counsel, Deputy Counsel from DTF, and staff at NYS Management and Budget to discuss Part NN about 1.5 weeks ago.
They didn't give anything away at the meeting so it is hard to say if this will be included in the budget or possibly brought back as a stand alone bill.  The politicians are feeling pressure from their Veteran constituents.  The Vets feel that December law
and February Chapter Amendment did not go far enough.  At this point it is a guess as to where this will come down.
I looked at the tax impact to my county.  Our county & town rates saw a minimal impact (>1%).  Obviously school will see a larger shift.
I will keep you posted on any updates.
Michael McGuire, IAO, CCD
Director
Albany County Real Property Tax Service Agency
112 State Street, Room 1103, Albany, NY 12207
tel   518 487-5292  fax  518 447-2503

subject: Re: GAR and Beacon
body:
We interviewed both GAR and Schneider, and we felt that Schneider was more prepared and offered more in their presentation.  A NJ company called Balcony
came in at the 11th hour and we almost switched to them, but then Schneider matched their price, and with Schneider already having all of our data (from SDG), we chose them.  Balcony then pulled some fast moves that I didn't like, and I let them
know about that, but that's a whole other conversation.
Since being with Schneider and having Beacon, we are thrilled.  Their service is hands on the best service we've ever experienced.  My two front end office
positions use Beacon a ton, and are constantly tweaking and changing things, little and big, and they respond immediately.
Go on our Beacon hub and look for a few properties and see what we have done.    Beacon
- Putnam County, NY - Property Search     We also got their upgraded maps package, which gave our parcel maps and up-glow with layers of great stuff--more than we
could have hoped for.
Clearly, we are VERY happy with Schneider!

So, we have Beacon and we have changed A LOT to work for us, as we have stand alone assessors, and I have to add a lot of notes so that the public can
be regularly updated with what is happening without files (we get databases only 4X/year).  We have re-ordered things, have requested some sections stay open, while others be collapsed, changed functions of adding sales, and the map and layers blow away what
we had with our former basic e-Parcel map setup.  They have now just added the 5217 button to the bottom of the property when you open it.
With Beacon, we put the most relevant sections to us up towards the top, we've added highlighting to notes, and we like that you just have to scroll down
to get to uploads, property card, tax map, and parcel map.  It's a one stop shop, whereas with IMO, there was a lot of clicking around to find things.
We're pretty happy.  T

subject: Re: Thoughts on Beacon?
body:
Cool, thanks. And taxpayers don't have issues with font size or menus at the top (some will take you to a page for the parcel you're on, some will take you to a general page like the folders with all the tax maps)? I know it's a personal preference to me to
have only the basics up front, with details behind clearly labeled menu options (or buttons, in IMO's case), rather than scrolling down to get to them, so maybe that's where my issue with the top bar comes in, lol.
I suppose we will have to see how it shakes out over the next 2 years. We already have a pretty comprehensive GIS site, so we just have a link to that from Beacon, so that's not a concern, but having an on-screen 5217 may be helpful.
Thanks everyone! I didn't know GAR had a similar service, so that's been interesting to peruse your sites lol.
~Kate
Kathleen Kearney, Director
Real Property Tax Services
Onondaga County
421 Montgomery St, 15th Floor
Syracuse, New York 13202
www.ongov.net/RPTS
P: (315) 435-2426
From: Real Property Tax Directors <RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US> on behalf of Patricia McLoughlin <Patricia.McLoughlin@PUTNAMCOUNTYNY.GOV>
Sent: Friday, October 17, 2025 3:17 PM
To: RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US <RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US>
Subject: Re: Thoughts on Beacon?
NOTICE: This email originated from
outside of Onondaga County's email system. Use caution with links and attachments.
So, we have Beacon and we have changed A LOT to work for us, as we have stand alone assessors, and I have to add a lot of notes so that the public can
be regularly updated with what is happening without files (we get databases only 4X/year).  We have re-ordered things, have requested some sections stay open, while others be collapsed, changed functions of adding sales, and the map and layers blow away what
we had with our former basic e-Parcel map setup.  They have now just added the 5217 button to the bottom of the property when you open it.
With Beacon, we put the most relevant sections to us up towards the top, we've added highlighting to notes, and we like that you just have to scroll
down to get to uploads, property card, tax map, and parcel map.  It's a one stop shop, whereas with IMO, there was a lot of clicking around to find things.
We're pretty happy.  T
Trish McLoughlin
Director  ● Office of Real Property Tax Services

PUTNAM COUNTY GOVERNMENT NEW YORK

So, we've got our testing site for Beacon and having not seen it before now because I'm new and was not involved in prior discussions, I am...underwhelmed. I know there aren't many good options besides self-design/hosting,
which I don't think our IT department would consider, lol, but I was hoping it would be something more modern looking and easy to read/understand. And I know it's not just Onondaga, I've looked at other counties to check the design, and it seems to be consistent.
Has anyone had other thoughts or discussions with them about this? I fully admit I could be an outlier, so I wanted to get others' opinions.
Thanks,
Kate

subject: Re: Thoughts on Beacon?
body:
So, we have Beacon and we have changed A LOT to work for us, as we have stand alone assessors, and I have to add a lot of notes so that the public can be
regularly updated with what is happening without files (we get databases only 4X/year).  We have re-ordered things, have requested some sections stay open, while others be collapsed, changed functions of adding sales, and the map and layers blow away what
we had with our former basic e-Parcel map setup.  They have now just added the 5217 button to the bottom of the property when you open it.
With Beacon, we put the most relevant sections to us up towards the top, we've added highlighting to notes, and we like that you just have to scroll down
to get to uploads, property card, tax map, and parcel map.  It's a one stop shop, whereas with IMO, there was a lot of clicking around to find things.
We're pretty happy.  T
Trish McLoughlin
Director  ● Office of Real Property Tax Services

subject: Grievance question
body:
Good morning and happy Monday....
In one of my towns, a property owner just passed away. He was the sole owner listed on his property. The son has approached the assessor to see if he will be able to contest his father's property value on
Grievance Day. According to the son, he and his brother are co-executors of their father's will.
Will the son (or the brother) be able to represent the property to contest it at Grievance, or would the estate have to be settled and a deed transfer filed?
Or, IF the will states who will inherit the property (not sure if it does), can that person represent the property prior to the deed transfer?
Will appreciate any thoughts.
Thanks!!
~ Meghan.

subject: Re: [ EXTERNAL ]  Re: Protected assessment data
body:
When it comes to FOIL requests they have their own set of laws. You cannot charge your typical fee for the 160d1 file if you have one. FOILing it is a legal loophole to this and the 160d1 file has to be provided. I have had to write a letter in regard to this
before. You have to redact phone numbers, email addresses, bank and escrow info, the internal notes, disability statuses, and your "protected people" such as judges, police officers, etc.
I would definitely reach out to your municipal attorney. Mine helped me a bunch with this.

subject: Re: (EXTERNAL) Board of Assessment Review
body:
Definitely have. What can you do? You can sue, but who wants to spend the money and also look bad going after a taxpayer for bad behavior. You can take to social media to argue your case, but you'll get roasted
to oblivion.
It will calm down eventually. They always do. I mean, you still will have your nuts that won't shutup, but the anger generally lessons.
Here's a line from a recent email to me, from an owner of a vacation property with 50 acres and a nice cabin:
"Why do I have to get harassed constantly?   Who can afford to pay the taxes to live here?  I work 50 hours a week to try and survive here
and you guys sit in an office and click buttons and raise everyone's taxes constantly and people cant afford to pay taxes that aren't accurate."
I reply trying to explain our assessing world. They then send multiple more emails because they now have my attention. I don't reply anymore. They go away.
Just tell the board members that it will eventually die down. Then argue the case with the BAR during the grievance for that person's property.
Another thing we now do is to take the impact notice tax information, color code a map with those that would have been higher, lower, and about the same. Then show that map to the residents/board
and say that you're not hearing from those that are staying the same or going down. Eye candy always helps.

subject: Enhance STAR renunciation
body:
I had an individual send in a renunciation due to a deceased parent (Jan 2024) but we received signed form a year later (2025).  We followed process with worksheet and sent "penalty" letter to individual, County Finance,
and ORPS. It is now being questioned by the individual.
I did discuss with the assessor and it should have been removed but I looked at the STAR report #1 which showed the deceased parent eligible so when running the batch file was added back in RPS.  Looks to be timeframe issue
across the board.
Being this is the situation as Director can I correct this withdrawing the penalty?
Sincerely-

body:

place.
The Town Supervisor just doesn't justify it. Gives her a few minutes at town minutes to speak. I have her on an appointment only basis. Again,  we don't encourage her in any way and hopefully she will find a new project soon.

body:

Learn why this is important

Tina
From: Real Property Tax Directors <RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US>
On Behalf Of Kathleen Kearney
Sent: Friday, October 17, 2025 2:01 PM
To: RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US
Subject: Thoughts on Beacon?
So, we've got our testing site for Beacon and having not seen it before now because I'm new and was not involved in prior discussions, I am...underwhelmed. I know there aren't many good options besides self-design/hosting,
which I don't think our IT department would consider, lol, but I was hoping it would be something more modern looking and easy to read/understand. And I know it's not just Onondaga, I've looked at other counties to check the design, and it seems to be consistent.
Has anyone had other thoughts or discussions with them about this? I fully admit I could be an outlier, so I wanted to get others' opinions.
Thanks,
Kate

subject: Agrivoltaics
body:
Happy Friday! I took a tour of a new agrivoltaics array in my county yesterday. It is pretty impressive, with tracking arrays set far enough apart that crops can be grown and harvested in between. I could see such hybrid sites being a good
compromise for keeping fields productive for agriculture while also providing electricity, as well as being a plus for farmers.
This may have been mentioned before, but what is your take on exemptions for solar and agriculture on the same footprint? Do you think that both exemptions can be applied, and, if not, exactly what would have to change to allow that? I
spoke with a few people, including one of the solar developers, people from the AFT, and a rep from NYSERDA, and everyone says that something needs to be done in Albany to fix this, but nothing formal seems to have been proposed.
Paul Wiley

subject: Thoughts on Beacon?
body:
So, we've got our testing site for Beacon and having not seen it before now because I'm new and was not involved in prior discussions, I am...underwhelmed. I know there aren't many good options besides self-design/hosting, which I don't think our IT department
would consider, lol, but I was hoping it would be something more modern looking and easy to read/understand. And I know it's not just Onondaga, I've looked at other counties to check the design, and it seems to be consistent. Has anyone had other thoughts
or discussions with them about this? I fully admit I could be an outlier, so I wanted to get others' opinions.
Thanks,
Kate
Kathleen Kearney, Director
Real Property Tax Services
Onondaga County
421 Montgomery St, 15th Floor
Syracuse, New York 13202
www.ongov.net/RPTS
P: (315) 435-2426

subject: Re: [External] Agrivoltaics
body:
No agland exemption can be granted.  The ag use is incidental to the use as an industrial power generator.
At least that was the determination by ORPTS when large scale solar started.  But with the push for renewable energy, it wouldn't surprise me to see ORPTS change their tune as directed from up above.
But until ORPTS issues an Opinion on this, I'll still not allow an exemption, and I'll still calculate a conversion penalty.  But then again, all my solar PILOTs (IDA PILOTS) exempt the land so the exemption
would only apply to fire district taxes.  It's almost a moot point here.
I'm surprised the state hasn't changed this already considering the solar lobby and the influence they had.  But until then...no exemption and conversion penalties are assessed.
Jay
