Thank you Jay, I get a little impatient reading these laws.
As per an earlier conversation/email thread, I see nowhere in this section that says anything about having a 100% disability rating as a necessity. I only see that the vet must
be "permanently and totally disabled". I have heard, not verified, that someone can be permanently and totally disabled without the 100% disability rating. It is counterintuitive but so is much of what we do.
11. In addition to any other exemption from taxation on real  property
which  may  be  allowed  to  veterans pursuant to the provisions of this
chapter, including subdivision three of section four hundred fifty-eight
of this title, a county, city, town,  village  or  school  district  may
adopt  a local law or resolution providing that the primary residence of
any seriously disabled veteran shall be fully exempt from  taxation  and
special  district  charges,  assessments  and special ad valorem levies,
provided that such veteran meets all other requirements of this  section
and  such  veteran  has  met  at  least one of the criteria set forth in
paragraph (a) of  this  subdivision  and  the  criterion  set  forth  in
paragraph  (b) of this subdivision. To be eligible for such exemption, a
veteran:
(a)(i) must have been discharged or  released  from  active  military,
naval,  space  or  air  service,  including  army and air national guard
service performed pursuant to federal  orders  under  title  10  of  the
United States code, under honorable conditions; or
(ii)  must  have  a qualifying condition, as defined in section one of
the veterans' services law, and must have  received  a  discharge  other
than bad conduct or dishonorable from such service; or
(iii)  must be a discharged LGBT veteran, as defined in section one of
the veterans' services law, and must have  received  a  discharge  other
than bad conduct or dishonorable from such service; and
(b)  must  be  considered  by the United States department of veterans
affairs to be permanently and totally disabled as a result  of  military
service, as evidenced by a letter, official form, or other document sent
to  such  veteran  from  such  department  that specifically states such
veteran is considered to be permanently and totally disabled as a result
of such service.
(c)  In  no case shall the taxable assessed value of the property of a
qualifying veteran be reduced below zero. Nothing contained herein shall
be construed to require or authorize the discontinuance of any exemption
granted  pursuant  to  subdivision  three  of   section   four   hundred
fifty-eight of this title.
(d)  Each county, city, town, village or school district that adopts a
local law or resolution for the exemption authorized by this subdivision
shall notify the department of veterans' services within thirty days  of
such   adoption;  provided,  however,  that  a  failure  to  notify  the
department of veterans' services within thirty  days  shall  not  render
such  local  law  or resolution ineffective. The department of veterans'
services shall compile and maintain a publicly available record of  each
such  county,  city,  town,  village or school district that has adopted
such exemption.

subject: Real Property Tax Law Section 581-A
body:
CAUTION:
I have a question about RPTL §581-a for an affordable housing complex.
We have a property that appears to qualify under §581-a. They submitted financial statements along with an income capitalization worksheet that concluded the property should receive a negative assessment. Our appraiser disagreed with
including several of their expenses in the calculation but they wouldn't budge. The Board of Assessment Review did not reduce the assessment, and the owner has now filed an Article 7 proceeding.
I'm trying to better understand what documentation typically require before adjusting an assessment under §581-a. Do we have to subtract ALL expenses to get the NOI or do you still follow what is used in the standard income approach?
I don't have a lot of experience with Article 7 or  581-a
Thank you,

11. In addition to any other exemption from taxation on real  property
which  may  be  allowed  to  veterans pursuant to the provisions of this
chapter, including subdivision three of section four hundred fifty-eight
of this title, a county, city, town,  village  or  school  district  may
adopt  a local law or resolution providing that the primary residence of
any seriously disabled veteran shall be fully exempt from  taxation  and
special  district  charges,  assessments  and special ad valorem levies,
provided that such veteran meets all other requirements of this  section
and  such  veteran  has  met  at  least one of the criteria set forth in
paragraph (a) of  this  subdivision  and  the  criterion  set  forth  in
paragraph  (b) of this subdivision. To be eligible for such exemption, a
veteran:
(a)(i) must have been discharged or  released  from  active  military,
naval,  space  or  air  service,  including  army and air national guard
service performed pursuant to federal  orders  under  title  10  of  the
United States code, under honorable conditions; or
(ii)  must  have  a qualifying condition, as defined in section one of
the veterans' services law, and must have  received  a  discharge  other
than bad conduct or dishonorable from such service; or
(iii)  must be a discharged LGBT veteran, as defined in section one of
the veterans' services law, and must have  received  a  discharge  other
than bad conduct or dishonorable from such service; and
(b)  must  be  considered  by the United States department of veterans
affairs to be permanently and totally disabled as a result  of  military
service, as evidenced by a letter, official form, or other document sent
to  such  veteran  from  such  department  that specifically states such
veteran is considered to be permanently and totally disabled as a result
of such service.
(c)  In  no case shall the taxable assessed value of the property of a
qualifying veteran be reduced below zero. Nothing contained herein shall
be construed to require or authorize the discontinuance of any exemption
granted  pursuant  to  subdivision  three  of   section   four   hundred
fifty-eight of this title.
(d)  Each county, city, town, village or school district that adopts a
local law or resolution for the exemption authorized by this subdivision
shall notify the department of veterans' services within thirty days  of
such   adoption;  provided,  however,  that  a  failure  to  notify  the
department of veterans' services within thirty  days  shall  not  render
such  local  law  or resolution ineffective. The department of veterans'
services shall compile and maintain a publicly available record of  each
such  county,  city,  town,  village or school district that has adopted
such exemption.

subject: Re: [EXTERNAL] [*Suspicious URL*] large Battery Energy Storage Facility PILOT
body:
CAUTION:
Good morning, Sherri,
We have three projects from one developer here in Orange County that went through the IDA for their PILOTs instead of going through the 487 exemption. Typically, for solar projects here in Orange County, we do the PILOTs here in Real Property
instead of going through the OC IDA. The developers convinced the IDA to ignore my income and cost analysis and instead give them a fifteen year PILOT using numbers they provided as if they were getting the 487 and based the income numbers on lower-priced
electric rates for other projects upstate instead of the higher-priced electric that we have around here, so that the base payments are $1,500 per MW of storage per year. I believe that the assessor set the assessment at something closer to the actual project
costs, so at least they are paying their share of special districts. I could share the PILOT with you if you want, but as I said these are unusual as they went through our IDA.
Fun fact: at least two of the projects burned, and I think one burned twice. And they started only around three  years ago.

subject: Re: Town Budgets
body:

We have an excel summary sheet that we send out to all the towns, (sample attached).  They have to enter their levy amounts and send it back with a physical copy of their budget.  We then go
through their budget to find all the numbers.  They also have to send us the fire and library budgets.  If something is amiss, we contact the town to get things clarified.

subject: Re: Known Pro Rata taxes?
body:
CAUTION:
If they are supposed to be taxable for 2026, the assessor can try to squeeze in with a 553.  It is a little close to the deadline for school since the assessor needs to send the form to the property
owner at least 10 days before the BAR meets.  Plus 553's are all supposed to be done 20 days before the issuance of the warrant.
Also I have never heard of billing omitted or pro-rated taxes outside of a tax bill especially since omitted amounts are supposed to be subtracted from the levy before calculating rates.

subject: Re: Known Pro Rata taxes?
body:
CAUTION:
Maybe it was only special district (unit-based) charges that were being discussed--I only remember thinking about it in reference to our sewer units, but now I can't for the life of me find the email.
And yeah, I don't know the legal logistics of what transpired between our IDA and the company, I just know when I met with the IDA earlier this year, they said that the company knew to expect a tax bill this fall and in January. Except on March 1st it
was still owned by the IDA, the sale hadn't happened yet (I didn't know that during my meeting). So, letter of the law, it's not taxable and not 553-eligible unless there is something I'm missing.
Kathleen Kearney, Director
Real Property Tax Services

421 Montgomery St, 15th Floor

outside of Onondaga County's email system. Use caution with links and attachments.
If they are supposed to be taxable for 2026, the assessor can try to squeeze in with a 553.  It is a little close to the deadline for school since the assessor needs to send the form to the
property owner at least 10 days before the BAR meets.  Plus 553's are all supposed to be done 20 days before the issuance of the warrant.
Also I have never heard of billing omitted or pro-rated taxes outside of a tax bill especially since omitted amounts are supposed to be subtracted from the levy before calculating rates.

body:

body:

As a newcomer (and someone who doesn't know much about this topic yet!), we have had this come up twice this year with our IDA.  So I'm thinking:
A private company buys a parcel that was IDA owned (Tax Roll 8) on August 1.  A tax bill needs to be generated and the private company needs to pay a pro-rated tax for August-December of current year.
Next year, an omitted tax is done for the pro-rated portion they paid, which would reduce the levy so nothing was collected over the levy amount.
Does that sound correct?  If not, any guidance would be much appreciated!
Thank you so much!

subject: Interest for changes after a certiorari decision?
body:
CAUTION:
I have a situation involving a Certiorari order. It's a long one, sorry, I'm just looking for opinions on whether I'm barking up the wrong tree (our attorney and finance office will do whatever they want, this is more for my education/confirmation)
Big Company filed a certiorari years ago. Order came out in 2021, and assessment should have stayed the same for 3 years. Normal stuff.
Assessor changed the assessment for the 2023 roll. Company got a change notice but didn't say anything until after 2023-4 school and 2024 Town/County taxes. Assessment was fixed for 2024 roll. I have no records
of a 556 being filed for any of the taxes they paid.
January 2026, their lawyer sent a huge packet, certified mail, demanding a refund (their calculations were wrong, but that's a sidenote). I guess they had already gotten something back directly from the town and
school. We replied that they should file a 556 form. Reached out to the assessor to tell them about it and ask for a 556 form. Nothing happened.
In June, they threatened the full weight of the courts if we continued to refuse to refund their money, WITH INTEREST. I'm not refusing anything, but this order from 2021 only refers to refunds prior to the order,
and we paid them. Get us the new form please.
Instead of filling out the 556, they have gone to a judge to get a new court order compelling us to pay, with interest, under the certiorari rules for calculating interest. Our attorney is fine with it, but on
principle I disagree. Once the original certiorari decision is finalized, the clock starts again, and we're back to business as usual. The court order from the certiorari is absolutely the REASON that the 556 refund should be granted, but we don't give interest
for that. The taxpayer knew their assessment was increased but chose not to ask us for a refund for over 2 years--we should not be penalized for that delay on their part.
Would you think that the certiorari interest rules would prevail here? Or standard 556 refund practices?
Thanks!
Kathleen Kearney, Director
Real Property Tax Services
Onondaga County
421 Montgomery St, 15th Floor
Syracuse, New York 13202
www.ongov.net/RPTS
P: (315) 435-2426

I have no records of a 556 being filed for any of the taxes they paid.
January 2026, their lawyer sent a huge packet, certified mail, demanding a refund (their calculations were wrong, but that's a sidenote). I guess they had already gotten something back directly
from the town and school. We replied that they should file a 556 form. Reached out to the assessor to tell them about it and ask for a 556 form. Nothing happened.
In June, they threatened the full weight of the courts if we continued to refuse to refund their money, WITH INTEREST. I'm not refusing anything, but this order from 2021 only refers to refunds
prior to the order, and we paid them. Get us the new form please.
Instead of filling out the 556, they have gone to a judge to get a new court order compelling us to pay, with interest, under the certiorari rules for calculating interest. Our attorney is fine
with it, but on principle I disagree. Once the original certiorari decision is finalized, the clock starts again, and we're back to business as usual. The court order from the certiorari is absolutely the REASON that the 556 refund should be granted, but we
don't give interest for that. The taxpayer knew their assessment was increased but chose not to ask us for a refund for over 2 years--we should not be penalized for that delay on their part.
Would you think that the certiorari interest rules would prevail here? Or standard 556 refund practices?
Thanks!

subject: Re: (EXTERNAL) Re: Interest for changes after a certiorari decision?
body:
CAUTION:
That old court order is done. It should now be a 556 (no interest) unless the assessment change was warranted. There are exceptions to the rule. 727 specifically says that it can be changed based on these
factors:
"(a) There is a revaluation or update  of  all  real  property  on  the
assessment roll;
(b)  There  is  a revaluation or update in a special assessing unit of
all real property of the same class;
(c) There has been a physical change (improvement) to the property;
(d) The zoning of such property has changed;
(e) Such property has been altered by fire, demolition, destruction or
similar catastrophe;
(f) An action has been taken by any office of the  federal,  state  or
local  government  which caused a discernible change in the general area
where the property is located which directly impacts on property values;
(g) There has been a change  in  the  occupancy  rate  of  twenty-five
percent  or  greater  in  a  building located on a property which is not
eligible for an assessment review under  title  one-A  of  this  article
(small claims assessment review);
(h)  The  owner  of  the  property  becomes  eligible or ineligible to
receive an exemption; or
(i)
The use or classification of the property has changed."
That's why this error goes through 556. You see if the assessor's change is warranted and make the recommendation.

subject: Re: Battery storage under RPTL 487
body:
CAUTION:
Those of you who have battery storage projects with 487 PILOTs, what rates per MW of storage are used for the PILOTs?
Paul Wiley
Director
Orange County Office of Real Property
255 Main St
Goshen, NY 10924
O: (845) 291-2494
C: (845) 806-0817
From: Wiley, Paul
Sent: Wednesday, May 20, 2026 12:56 PM
To: Real Property Tax Directors <RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US>
Subject: Battery storage under RPTL 487
Hey all,
I had thought that battery storage had to be in conjunction with a solar or other alternative energy source to get a PILOT under 487, but in re-reading the law, it looks like battery storage connected to the grid is eligible for a PILOT
even without being part of a solar project, because it says "or" below. Am I reading that right?
"Real property that contains a solar energy, wind energy, farm waste energy, micro-hydroelectric energy, fuel cell electric generating, micro-combined heat and power generating equipment, or an electric energy storage system approved by
the State Energy Research and Development Authority is exempt from taxation for a period of 15 years to the extent of any increase in assessed value due to the system. Such property is liable for special ad valorem levies and special assessments. The exemption
as reenacted in 1990 is subject to local option."
https://www.tax.ny.gov/research/property/assess/manuals/vol4/pt1/sec4_01/sec487.htm
We have some battery storage connected to solar projects that are part of PILOTs done before I started here, and we have three battery storage projects that went through our IDA to get IDA PILOTs (still not happy about that, but I have
been able to contain my anger into a slow simmer, so I have that going for me). But we have not had any battery projects asking for 487 PILOTs-- until now.
And what rate are you all doing battery storage? We had done the solar ones at $4,000 per MW of storage, compared to the $10,000 per MW that we get for solar (Central Hudson and Orange & Rockland have some of the highest rates this side
of Hawaii, so it justifies the high PILOT rates. Don't at me, y'all).
Paul Wiley

Goshen, NY 10924

subject: Re: Solar Win!
body:
CAUTION:
Don't forget that the law (RPTL 497) was changed so that this decision reflects the intent of the new law.
The 3rd department had ruled differently in the
Laertes vs Harford case.  Hopefully these 2 decisions are the last cases from the prior law.
At the time of the Laertes case, NYSERDA never kept a record of who submitted legislation to them.  NYSERDA simply linked to the ORPTS website.  I'm not sure if NYSERDA keeps a record now or not.  And ORPTS never realized that school districts
can cross over county boundaries.  Even today, school districts that cross county boundaries are not listed correctly on ORPTS website.  I have countless emails to ORPTS legal/communications to correct it - but it never happened.  I simply had to give up as

subject: Fall Conference Check-In & Registration
body:
Folks,
Our conference is less than a week away!  I hope that you are excited and looking forward to this event.  Don't forget your Halloween Costumes for Monday night!
You can check into the hotel starting at 4pm.  Conference registration will be available on Sunday from 4-5:30pm and Monday from 8-9am.  Check-in and registration will be at The Inn.  Parking is located 0.4 miles from The Inn.  Please check
in, drop your bags, and then move your car to the parking lot.  If you would like transportation from the parking lot back to The Inn please let Silver Bay staff know upon checking in.
See you all in a few days!
Michael McGuire, IAO, CCD
Director

112 State Street, Room 1103, Albany, NY 12207

subject: Re: COE
body:
CAUTION:
Because the application is kind of vague and you may want to do some due diligence, I would ask the property owner for their proof that there was an error.  Proof from the property owner is a
requirement in the law.  You may also want to get a statement from the assessor that they believe that the assessment was correct for the last 3 years.
Either way, "non-uniform assessment" is not defined as a correctable error in the law and they should have gone to grievance.  It doesn't matter that they went this year since each roll is separate.
This would be the same as if they caught a mistake in the description of the property.  It can only be fixed going forward.

subject: Re: (EXTERNAL) FOIL Request
body:
CAUTION:
You don't have to create anything new for FOIL. The RPS.db can get scrubbed using the state's FOIL tool (if it still works). You can also remove all the usernames/passwords and give them the db with just a
generic one.
Here's the kicker, the requester doesn't understand their own request. The db is not a flat file like a csv/Excel is. It's a file that has hundreds of tables that point to hundreds of tables. The FOIL requester
will get a useless file basically. Years ago I found a free utility that could read a Sybase db (that's what it is), but I have no idea if that's even around anymore.

Trish,
We only get deeds after they are recorded and are constantly reaching out to attorney offices and verifying the information.  I leave it up to them to decide if they want a corrective
deed.  We can only advise them of the potential flag by NYS.
Additionally, we are frequently finding title errors especially when parcels have been combined and a deed comes in describing only a portion of the property but the 5217 shows intent
to convey the entire parcel...so frustrating!  Are attorneys even looking at these descriptions any more?
Candy Akin, CCD
Real Property Tax Director
O: 315-376-5336

candyakin@lewiscounty.ny.gov
7660 North State St. | Lowville, NY 13367
From: Real Property Tax Directors <RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US>
On Behalf Of Patricia McLoughlin
Sent: Thursday, October 9, 2025 2:01 PM
To: RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US
Subject: Deed Question
Hello,
We are finding more than a few mistakes on deeds as they come to our office AFTER being filed.  Example, one today that showed sales price of $310,000 on the
5217, yet consideration of $700,000.  My clerk called the attorney and asked why the difference, and they realized it was a typo--should be $310,000.  We asked that they do a deed correction, and they are asking--why didn't we 'catch it'.  We said, WE JUST DID!
We don't get to see them before they get filed.  They need to do a deed correction, as the State will flag this if we send it up AS IS.
Do you all get your deeds and 5217's AFTER they have been filed?  Do you bother reaching out to attorneys when you find mistakes?
Our town is not used to our office calling out mistakes--but we are finding a fair amount of them--as we have a new clerk who is a title searcher and knows this
stuff like the back of her hand, and our former clerk did not.  Everything basically went through as is before.
Thoughts?  T
Trish McLoughlin

PUTNAM COUNTY GOVERNMENT NEW YORK

subject: Re: Deed Question
body:
Trish,
We only get deeds after they are recorded and are constantly reaching out to attorney offices and verifying the information.  I leave it up to them to decide if they want a corrective
deed.  We can only advise them of the potential flag by NYS.
Additionally, we are frequently finding title errors especially when parcels have been combined and a deed comes in describing only a portion of the property but the 5217 shows intent
to convey the entire parcel...so frustrating!  Are attorneys even looking at these descriptions any more?
Candy Akin, CCD
Real Property Tax Director
O: 315-376-5336
M: 315-907-2032
candyakin@lewiscounty.ny.gov
7660 North State St. | Lowville, NY 13367
From: Real Property Tax Directors <RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US>
On Behalf Of Patricia McLoughlin
Sent: Thursday, October 9, 2025 2:01 PM
To: RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US
Subject: Deed Question
Hello,
We are finding more than a few mistakes on deeds as they come to our office AFTER being filed.  Example, one today that showed sales price of $310,000 on the
5217, yet consideration of $700,000.  My clerk called the attorney and asked why the difference, and they realized it was a typo--should be $310,000.  We asked that they do a deed correction, and they are asking--why didn't we 'catch it'.  We said, WE JUST DID!
We don't get to see them before they get filed.  They need to do a deed correction, as the State will flag this if we send it up AS IS.
Do you all get your deeds and 5217's AFTER they have been filed?  Do you bother reaching out to attorneys when you find mistakes?
Our town is not used to our office calling out mistakes--but we are finding a fair amount of them--as we have a new clerk who is a title searcher and knows this
stuff like the back of her hand, and our former clerk did not.  Everything basically went through as is before.
Thoughts?  T
Trish McLoughlin
Director  ● Office of Real Property Tax Services
PHONE | 845.808.1000 ● X-49315 | WEBSITE |
PUTNAMCOUNTYNY.COM
PUTNAM COUNTY GOVERNMENT NEW YORK
"Empowering Putnam County through dedicated service."

subject: Tax mapping question
body:
CAUTION:
We had a town approve a subdivision map merging 39 parcels into one massive parcel. Unfortunately, the area is too large for our Auto-CAD to process it because crosses FIVE map sections. This is a suburban town with the most parcels in the county and the highest
density--that many acres may be fine for a single parcel in another town, but not how this one is laid out (that is my understanding of the issue, but it only became an issue right as folks were leaving for the day). The assessor is adamant that we have to
figure out how to make it work to make it a single parcel because "it's a legal process" that we don't have an option to change. We haven't fully switched over to GIS yet, but our current thought is to skip the normal Auto-CAD entirely to remove the physical
area limitation and then give it its own map section maybe (that was my suggestion, but I'm not a mapper, so that's a tomorrow discussion). However, if that doesn't work, how would y'all suggest handling this? Are we locked in to re-create entire map sections
because the town's zoning board allowed the merge and a subdivision map was filed? We've suggested one parcel per section, but this is unacceptable.
I'm sure we can figure it out but given this particular assessor's distasteful attitude toward my staff and our office in general on a regular basis, we are less inclined to go through a significant remapping effort if we don't have to, and I get lost in all
the tax mapping stuff because it's spread over laws/rules/unofficial guidance/etc.
Thanks y'all!
Kathleen Kearney, Director
Real Property Tax Services
Onondaga County
421 Montgomery St, 15th Floor
Syracuse, New York 13202
www.ongov.net/RPTS
P: (315) 435-2426

subject: 100% Vet and Schools
body:
CAUTION:
I'm finishing up my loss taxable report and something just occurred to me. The State will make money off of the 100% vet exemption if any schools grant it. They will have less to pay back to them due to all the STAR exemptions being removed.
It will be a double-hit to those taxpayers in those districts. They will lose taxable and their school will get less STAR money back.
I wonder how the state will track the STAR Credit Check with this. They will have to run their checks by the final rolls to see if anyone is paying zero school taxes now.
As an aside, we have identified 104 parcels within my county of 52,000+ that would be eligible. That's according to my data and our VA combining through it.
Daniel T. Martonis, CCD
Director of Real Property Tax Services
Chair, Cattaraugus County Land Bank
Board Chair, NYSACDRPTS
Cattaraugus County
Real Property Tax Services
207 Rock City Street, Suite 101
Little Valley, NY 14755

Fax: (716) 938-2758

Good morning --
I hope that this message finds you safe and well.
We have an important update regarding the new local option for a full property tax exemption for Veterans who have a 100% permanent and total VA rating.
After engaging in deliberations with the New York State Department of Taxation & Finance, I am pleased to report that Veterans who have a permanent and total designation from the VA accompanying a finding of Total Disability based on Individual
Unemployability (TDIU) will now also be eligible for this exemption in jurisdictions that "opt in" to provide it.
This means that there are two pathways for a Veteran to qualify in jurisdictions that opt in:
(1) A 100% rating with a permanent and total designation from the United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA); or
(2) A finding of TDIU from the VA with a permanent and total designation.
The crucial element in both cases is the "permanent and totally disabling" finding by VA, holding that the medical condition(s) is unlikely to improve during that Veteran's lifetime. A plain 100%, or a plain TDIU designation, will not qualify.
The finding of "permanent and totally disabling" must be present.
Under 38 C.F.R. 3.340, a Veteran can have a 100% rating or a designation of individual unemployability -- and still receive a letter from the VA stating that they are permanently and totally disabled if the VA
deems their condition(s) unlikely to ever medically improve.
It is under this rationale that both of the above-described pathways can lead to the full property tax exemption in a jurisdiction that opts in under this new law. There is no limit to "100% permanently and totally
disabled" Veterans. "TDIU permanent and total"-rated Veterans qualify as well.
Please let me know if you have any questions regarding this, and I will be glad to answer to the best of my ability.
Many thanks!
Respectfully,
Benjamin P. Pomerance

subject: Re: postmarks and the post office
body:
State Law allows the tax collector to waive the penalties if it is the interest of the municipality. Have the Supervisor along with
his Board create a resolution to say that it is in the interest of the municipality
RPT § 1182. Cancellation or reduction of interest, penalties and other charges
If the governing body of any tax district shall determine that it is for the
best interests of the tax district, it shall have the power, by resolution, to authorize the enforcing officer to permit the cancellation in whole or in part of any interest, penalties or other charges imposed by law to which the tax district or any
other municipal corporation shall be lawfully entitled; provided, however, that in cases where such interest, penalties, or other charges, if collected by the tax district, belong to a municipal corporation therein, no reduction or remission in whole or in
part of such interest, penalties, or other charges shall be made without the consent of the municipal corporation affected, which consent may be given by resolution adopted after a public hearing.

PUTNAM COUNTY NOTICE
THIS EMAIL IS FROM AN EXTERNAL SENDER! DO
NOT click links, DO NOT open attachments, DO NOT forward if you were not expecting this email or if it seems suspicious in any way! REMEMBER: NEVER provide your user ID or password to anyone for any reason!
Hi T!
I am running into an issue, and I wonder if this could be a topic of discussion for next School collection.
We had about 15 people who say they walked into the post office on September 30 to hand in their tax payments.
Per my conversation with the Brewster Post Office, they DO not postmark in Brewster, but these envelopes go to White Plains where they are postmarked.
In almost all the referred to 15, the postmark was Oct 1,
after the deadline.
We returned the payments for lack of valid Sept 30 postmarks which, is exactly what I am supposed to do.
My problem is that I did not know this was the case with the post office, my husband says he also was unaware of this, and all these taxpayers are probably going to feel the same.
I am resigned to not being able to help these 15, its just tax law, however, I warned my supervisor he may get some blow back and I am leaving on vacation. Unintentional fabulous timing for me....
T/Supervisor thinks, and I agree, that we may want to somehow supply this information to the taxpayer more specifically regarding the way our local post
office handles (or rather doesn't) postmarks and that the valid postmarks come from Westchester likely the next day or after.
What do you think?
Thanks so much,
AnnMarie
Receiver of Taxes

subject: Library Appropriation in Town Budget
body:
CAUTION:
Hi there,
I have a town that has an appropriation for a library and is on the tax bill as a breakout of town's general fund.  When the library wants to change the amount, they go to referendum at the general election.
This year, the town is going to pass their budget before the general election and use the appropriation amount voted on last year based on Education Law §259(1)(b) which states, "An increase in library funding provided pursuant to this paragraph shall not
apply to a municipal budget adopted prior to the date of such election."
The library is asking me if I will change the amount to be collected if they provide me with the election results before I calculate tax rates.  My gut is that I cannot do that because I don't have the authority
to change the town's budget amounts in this way.
Has anyone had this happen before?
Cathy Weisse
Director of Real Property Tax Services
Dutchess County Real Property Tax Service Agency
22 Market Street
Poughkeepsie, NY  12601

body:
Busy day time from me!  Thoughts on this sitch?  T
Trish McLoughlin
Director  ● Office of Real Property Tax Services

To: Patricia McLoughlin <Patricia.McLoughlin@putnamcountyny.gov>
Subject: postmarks and the post office
PUTNAM COUNTY NOTICE
THIS EMAIL IS FROM AN EXTERNAL SENDER! DO
NOT click links, DO NOT open attachments, DO NOT forward if you were not expecting this email or if it seems suspicious in any way! REMEMBER: NEVER provide your user ID or password to anyone for any reason!
Hi T!
I am running into an issue, and I wonder if this could be a topic of discussion for next School collection.
We had about 15 people who say they walked into the post office on September 30 to hand in their tax payments.
Per my conversation with the Brewster Post Office, they DO not postmark in Brewster, but these envelopes go to White Plains where they are postmarked.
In almost all the referred to 15, the postmark was Oct 1,
after the deadline.
We returned the payments for lack of valid Sept 30 postmarks which, is exactly what I am supposed to do.
My problem is that I did not know this was the case with the post office, my husband says he also was unaware of this, and all these taxpayers are probably going to feel the same.
I am resigned to not being able to help these 15, its just tax law, however, I warned my supervisor he may get some blow back and I am leaving on vacation. Unintentional fabulous timing for me....
T/Supervisor thinks, and I agree, that we may want to somehow supply this information to the taxpayer more specifically regarding the way our local post
office handles (or rather doesn't) postmarks and that the valid postmarks come from Westchester likely the next day or after.
What do you think?
Thanks so much,
AnnMarie
Receiver of Taxes

Subject: Library Appropriation in Town Budget
WARNING - This email was sent from outside of this organization. Take care when opening links or attachments from external sources.
Hi there,
I have a town that has an appropriation for a library and is on the tax bill as a breakout of town's general fund.  When the library wants to change the
amount, they go to referendum at the general election.  This year, the town is going to pass their budget before the general election and use the appropriation amount voted on last year based on Education Law §259(1)(b) which states, "An increase in library
funding provided pursuant to this paragraph shall not apply to a municipal budget adopted prior to the date of such election."
The library is asking me if I will change the amount to be collected if they provide me with the election results before I calculate tax rates.  My gut is
that I cannot do that because I don't have the authority to change the town's budget amounts in this way.
Has anyone had this happen before?
Cathy Weisse

So, I had a school district call me to confirm one of my town's eq rates, as it is not at 100%.  I have gotten several emails from ORPTS stating, since June,
that it is at 90%.  The school district said that the website said 98%, which was their last year's eq rate.  I told her that it is 90 for 2026.
She has now been informed by ORPTS that she should have used 98, as that was what was on the website.  I was always told that you use the more current letter
from ORPTS if you get one, over what the website might say.  My ORPTS team is now telling me that she should have used the 2025 98%, because it said Final on the website.  I really don't understand this, as I got the attached in June that said 90.  Why, in
August, would we not use that eq rate?

The STAR reimbursement application for a segment of 1 school district is doubling the STAR reimbursement amount granted and throwing off the reconciliation for the school district.

I check the tax roll and the exemption amount applied to each parcel receiving the exemption is correct.

subject: correction?
body:
CAUTION:
Good afternoon, all... Happy Friday (finally) -
The assessor just found out from a property owner that a R/S 8 Wholly Exempt property that they own is being rented out and should be R/S 1 taxable.
It is too late to correct this for the school tax roll. Would I be correct that the best course of action would be to have the assessor fill out a RP-553 between 10/3-12/11 to correct prior to the town/county taxes as an Omission (4-A)(2),
and then do omitted taxes for the school to go on their tax bill next year?
Thoughts?

Meghan.

subject: Re: School Taxable values not matching
body:
CAUTION:
I have a few instances where the assessment roll totals simply do not match the totals in the standard reports within RPS.  School taxable, town taxable, and fire district taxable values are all off.  The
totals within RPS seem to be the correct totals - the rolls are not.  These are just RPS
errors 'enhancements' - it's not like you can call the vendor and have them fix it.  You must learn to live with them.
But I would run a report from the final roll (you should have a copy from sending to NYS)...and a report from the current roll.  I then link the two reports by the parcel via MSAccess and find the differences
in the school taxable.
I have a school bill where there is 1 senior exemption in it - it doesn't show on the tax files.  I simply just do a correction each year for it.  The owner knows it is a state database problem, so they just
send us their bill each year and we do a correction.  It's just 1 parcel so it's not that much of an issue for the school.
Jay

Caution: This is an external email. Please take care when clicking links or opening attachments. When in doubt, contact the Help Desk.
Getting back on this:  turns out I have 3 school districts that go into Westchester, and because Westchester is on a different Final Roll schedule than
our county (they don't do theirs until Sept 1), we have to go with THEIR rate, which for us is last year's--but just for those 3 school districts.  Everyone else is at current.
This was quite the debacle this year for us, as one of my towns dropped from 100 to 98 last year, and is now down to 90, and I told the district when they
called and asked, that that town's eq rate is 90, so they used it.  It was realized prior to the bills going out, but AFTER they were printed, that because they go into Westchester, they have different rules, which I never knew.
Same goes for those special eq rate letters that I had sent out and had questions on.  I was told by ORPTS that if the 'purpose' on these letters says for
'use for school apportioning', then we use those rates for districts that have those towns in them.  Soooo, I sent those letters over to the districts that had a particular town that got the special rate.  WELL, ORPTS forgot to mention that the fine print
of the Purpose section that refers you to the RP law, states that ONLY where your district goes into another county--YES, Westchester again!!!  So
ONLY the districts that have this town in it THAT GO INTO WESTCHESTER would use this special eq rate, everyone else would use current!  So, 2 more districts bit the dust and needed to be reprinted.  It's been a crazy ride.  But new lessons learned for
me.  Never knew about this whole Westchester thing!
Thanks Vic!!!

Getting back on this:  turns out I have 3 school districts that go into Westchester, and because Westchester is on a different Final Roll schedule than
our county (they don't do theirs until Sept 1), we have to go with THEIR rate, which for us is last year's--but just for those 3 school districts.  Everyone else is at current.
This was quite the debacle this year for us, as one of my towns dropped from 100 to 98 last year, and is now down to 90, and I told the district when they
called and asked, that that town's eq rate is 90, so they used it.  It was realized prior to the bills going out, but AFTER they were printed, that because they go into Westchester, they have different rules, which I never knew.
Same goes for those special eq rate letters that I had sent out and had questions on.  I was told by ORPTS that if the 'purpose' on these letters says for
'use for school apportioning', then we use those rates for districts that have those towns in them.  Soooo, I sent those letters over to the districts that had a particular town that got the special rate.  WELL, ORPTS forgot to mention that the fine print
of the Purpose section that refers you to the RP law, states that ONLY where your district goes into another county--YES, Westchester again!!!  So
ONLY the districts that have this town in it THAT GO INTO WESTCHESTER would use this special eq rate, everyone else would use current!  So, 2 more districts bit the dust and needed to be reprinted.  It's been a crazy ride.  But new lessons learned for
me.  Never knew about this whole Westchester thing!
Thanks Vic!!!
Trish McLoughlin

Date:        08/17/2026 04:18 PM
Subject:        Tax mapping question
Sent by:        "Real Property Tax Directors" <RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US>
We had a town approve a subdivision map merging 39 parcels into one massive parcel. Unfortunately, the area is too large for our Auto-CAD to process it because crosses FIVE map sections. This is a suburban town with the most parcels in the county and the highest
density--that many acres may be fine for a single parcel in another town, but not how this one is laid out (that is my understanding of the issue, but it only became an issue right as folks were leaving for the day). The assessor is adamant that we have to
figure out how to make it work to make it a single parcel because "it's a legal process" that we don't have an option to change. We haven't fully switched over to GIS yet, but our current thought is to skip the normal Auto-CAD entirely to remove the physical
area limitation and then give it its own map section maybe (that was my suggestion, but I'm not a mapper, so that's a tomorrow discussion). However, if that doesn't work, how would y'all suggest handling this? Are we locked in to re-create entire map sections
because the town's zoning board allowed the merge and a subdivision map was filed? We've suggested one parcel per section, but this is unacceptable.
I'm sure we can figure it out but given this particular assessor's distasteful attitude toward my staff and our office in general on a regular basis, we are less inclined to go through a significant remapping effort if we don't have to, and I get lost in all
the tax mapping stuff because it's spread over laws/rules/unofficial guidance/etc.
Thanks y'all!
Kathleen Kearney, Director
Real Property Tax Services
Onondaga County
421 Montgomery St, 15th Floor
Syracuse, New York 13202
www.ongov.net/RPTS
P: (315) 435-2426

subject: Re: (EXTERNAL) Re: STAR
body:
CAUTION:
I'll add in my two cents (aka rant). Since this came out I have only ever emailed to that email address (or given a link to download them). I have never once filled
out the cover sheet. This is a state "mandate" if you will and I refuse to make life easier for them since they don't for me.
I would like to see a united front. We all stop jumping through hoops for them. They continue to make our lives harder, not easier, but then expect use to constantly
help them out.
They used to give us money for maintaining the STAR. They used to give us money for scanning sales. Now it's all gone and all we are left with is more work for no money.
I want to go back to sending them all paper everything. Let's see how fast they cave.
Old grumpy guy...out!

Date:        08/17/2026 04:18 PM
Subject:        Tax mapping question
Sent by:        "Real Property Tax Directors" <RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US>
We had a town approve a subdivision map merging 39 parcels into one massive parcel. Unfortunately, the area is too large for our Auto-CAD to process it because crosses FIVE map sections. This is a suburban town with the most parcels in the county and the highest
density--that many acres may be fine for a single parcel in another town, but not how this one is laid out (that is my understanding of the issue, but it only became an issue right as folks were leaving for the day). The assessor is adamant that we have to
figure out how to make it work to make it a single parcel because "it's a legal process" that we don't have an option to change. We haven't fully switched over to GIS yet, but our current thought is to skip the normal Auto-CAD entirely to remove the physical
area limitation and then give it its own map section maybe (that was my suggestion, but I'm not a mapper, so that's a tomorrow discussion). However, if that doesn't work, how would y'all suggest handling this? Are we locked in to re-create entire map sections
because the town's zoning board allowed the merge and a subdivision map was filed? We've suggested one parcel per section, but this is unacceptable.
I'm sure we can figure it out but given this particular assessor's distasteful attitude toward my staff and our office in general on a regular basis, we are less inclined to go through a significant remapping effort if we don't have to, and I get lost in all
the tax mapping stuff because it's spread over laws/rules/unofficial guidance/etc.
Thanks y'all!
Kathleen Kearney, Director
Real Property Tax Services
Onondaga County
421 Montgomery St, 15th Floor
Syracuse, New York 13202
www.ongov.net/RPTS

subject: Tax Data Verification Webinar
body:
CAUTION:
Good morning all,
Here is a link to a webinar from the NYS Comptroller's office about a Tax Data Verification Webinar.
Registration
Here's the writeup:
The Local Government Tax Data Verification system (LGTDV) is a secure web application where Counties (and towns and cities in Westchester County) can report and review their real property tax roll information.
Once reported through the Tax Data Verification system, the data is reviewed by OSC staff before being published to the Real Property Tax Levies, Taxable Full Value and Full Value Tax Rates page on the Office of the State Comptroller website. OSC staff will
discuss the tax roll collection process, review process, and how the data is used. Any local officials who provide OSC with tax roll information are invited. (Live captioning available)
I forget when we worked with the NYS Comptroller's office to help design this new system but it's so much easier than the old MA-14E (if you never filled out the MA-14E, you are lucky).  But we finally got
them to use the 160 files that we send to the state to prepopulate much of this data.
Jay

subject: Address Changes for Properties
body:
CAUTION:
How does your County handle address changes for properties?
Currently, we have an address change form for LLC, Company, Trust, etc. which requires the person signing the form to have it notarized and states "Under penalties of perjury,
I certify to the best of my knowledge and belief that this report is true, correct, and complete, and that I am solely authorized to report address changes."
The other properties that are owned by and individuals requires a signature but not a notarization. Also electronic signatures are not allowed.
Thank you
Tammy Lacey, CCD

subject: Re: EXTERNAL Re: Deed Question
body:
The 5217 is a tax form.  It has no bearing on the information contained within the deed.  There is no way to correct a 5217 without
recording a new deed - however there really is no reason to try and force that a correct 5217 be filed.  As noted by others, corrected information should be entered into RPS and reported as part of the sales reporting process.
If there are errors in deeds we will reach out to the attorney and strongly suggest that a corrected deed be filed.  Deed errors can
cause title issues in the future.

We get the deed transfers after they have been filed at the County Clerk's office...

pretty much everything and anything...). The only thing that our Clerk's office will adjust is the top section (date deed recorded, SWIS code).
We use Salescan and will put the CORRECT info for the RP-5217 into that when we enter the sale. We will also rescan it to send to the assessor so
they see the corrections, as well.

will call for clarification or to request a correction deed.

Hello,
We are finding more than a few mistakes on deeds as they come to our office AFTER being filed.  Example, one today that showed sales price of $310,000 on the
5217, yet consideration of $700,000.  My clerk called the attorney and asked why the difference, and they realized it was a typo--should be $310,000.  We asked that they do a deed correction, and they are asking--why didn't we 'catch it'.  We said, WE JUST DID!
We don't get to see them before they get filed.  They need to do a deed correction, as the State will flag this if we send it up AS IS.
Do you all get your deeds and 5217's AFTER they have been filed?  Do you bother reaching out to attorneys when you find mistakes?
Our town is not used to our office calling out mistakes--but we are finding a fair amount of them--as we have a new clerk who is a title searcher and knows this
stuff like the back of her hand, and our former clerk did not.  Everything basically went through as is before.
Thoughts?  T

subject: Re: Deed Question
body:
We get the deed transfers after they have been filed at the County Clerk's office...
Are you finding errors in the deed itself or just on the RP-5217? The 5217 is constantly strewn with errors (wrong school district, parcel address,
pretty much everything and anything...). The only thing that our Clerk's office will adjust is the top section (date deed recorded, SWIS code).
We use Salescan and will put the CORRECT info for the RP-5217 into that when we enter the sale. We will also rescan it to send to the assessor so
they see the corrections, as well.
For the most part, the main thing that the attorney gets called for is because the description is incorrect IN THE DEED ITSELF and my tax mapper
will call for clarification or to request a correction deed.
Occasionally, we will call about other things (says Life Use on 5217, but not in the deed), but most often it's description related.
If I called them every time the 5217 was incorrect, I'd never be off of the phone!!! LOL
See everyone in a couple of weeks!!
~ Meg.
Meghan K. Kincaid

Sent: Thursday, October 09, 2025 2:01 PM
To: RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US
Subject: Deed Question
Hello,
We are finding more than a few mistakes on deeds as they come to our office AFTER being filed.  Example, one today that showed sales price of $310,000 on the
5217, yet consideration of $700,000.  My clerk called the attorney and asked why the difference, and they realized it was a typo--should be $310,000.  We asked that they do a deed correction, and they are asking--why didn't we 'catch it'.  We said, WE JUST DID!
We don't get to see them before they get filed.  They need to do a deed correction, as the State will flag this if we send it up AS IS.
Do you all get your deeds and 5217's AFTER they have been filed?  Do you bother reaching out to attorneys when you find mistakes?
Our town is not used to our office calling out mistakes--but we are finding a fair amount of them--as we have a new clerk who is a title searcher and knows this
stuff like the back of her hand, and our former clerk did not.  Everything basically went through as is before.
Thoughts?  T
Trish McLoughlin

body:
We get the deeds after they have been filed, and then we verify the buyers, sellers, property description, etc. There are a surprising number of errors in filed deeds, and we have been working with our county clerk to get the people that accept the deeds to at least make sure that the names seem to match the info on the 5217 and that there is a Schedule A property description so that we can check it after it is filed. We have a lot of deeds in limbo pending response by the buyers or the attorneys to confirm certain missing or incorrect info.
Paul Wiley
Director

255 Main St
Goshen, NY 10924
(845) 291-2494
From: Real Property Tax Directors <RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US> On Behalf Of Patricia McLoughlin
Sent: Thursday, October 9, 2025 2:01 PM
To: RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US
Subject: [EXTERNAL] Deed Question
Hello, We are finding more than a few mistakes on deeds as they come to our office AFTER being filed. Example, one today that showed sales price of $310,000 on the 5217, yet consideration of $700,000.
sophospsmartbannerend
Hello,
We are finding more than a few mistakes on deeds as they come to our office AFTER being filed.  Example, one today that showed sales price of $310,000 on the 5217, yet consideration of $700,000.  My clerk called the attorney and asked why the difference, and they realized it was a typo―should be $310,000.  We asked that they do a deed correction, and they are asking―why didn't we 'catch it'.  We said, WE JUST DID!  We don't get to see them before they get filed.  They need to do a deed correction, as the State will flag this if we send it up AS IS.
Do you all get your deeds and 5217's AFTER they have been filed?  Do you bother reaching out to attorneys when you find mistakes?
Our town is not used to our office calling out mistakes―but we are finding a fair amount of them―as we have a new clerk who is a title searcher and knows this stuff like the back of her hand, and our former clerk did not.  Everything basically went through as is before.
Thoughts?  T
Trish McLoughlin

Free Webinar
Understanding the New Disabled Veterans Exemption
Friday, September 11, 2026  10:00 - 11:00 a.m.
Recent changes to RPTL §458-a have generated considerable discussion and, understandably, considerable
confusion regarding the new property tax exemption for certain permanently and totally disabled veterans.
Join
Benjamin Pomerance, Deputy Counsel for the New York State Department of Veterans'
Services, for a brief webinar discussing the recent legislative changes,
the veterans affected by them, and the Department's perspective on the new exemption.
With formal administrative guidance from the New York State Office of Real Property Tax Services (ORPTS)
still forthcoming, this webinar provides assessors with an opportunity to better understand the legislation and its evolution while we await additional guidance regarding its implementation.
An Important Note for Assessors:
This webinar is being offered for informational and educational purposes. Mr. Pomerance represents the New York State Department of Veterans' Services and will be presenting the legislation from the perspective of that agency and the veterans it serves.
As assessors, our responsibility is different. We do not write the law or determine the policy behind it,
nor is our role to decide whether an exemption is fair or appropriate. Our responsibility is to understand the law as enacted and administer it accurately, consistently, and professionally.
Please note:
The information presented will reflect the law and available guidance as understood at the time of the webinar. Additional guidance from ORPTS, subsequent legislative action, or other developments may affect how the exemption is ultimately administered. NYSAA
will continue to provide updates to its membership as additional information becomes available.
This webinar is intended to help assessors better understand the legislation, the perspective of the veterans
it affects, and the issues surrounding its implementation as we prepare to administer the changes to RPTL §458-a.
Scott Shedler, IAO, will also provide some relevant updates as it relates to assessors and the small claims
assessment review (SCAR).  This promises to be a very informative webinar. No CE credit is awarded for webinars.
As always, at the conclusion of the webinar, one lucky member will win a $25 gift card. You must be present
to win.
One-Day Seminars
Income Approach Case Study
September 9, 2026  9:00 a.m. - 4:00 p.m.
Instructor: Edye McCarthy, FIAO
6 CE credits
Understanding how a property generates income is often the truest key to unlocking its actual value.
The Income Approach: Demystifying the math and methodology,
is a comprehensive workshop designed to demystify the mechanics of income capitalization and present tools to confidently value income-producing properties. This workshop approaches valuation from the ground up, treating the Income Approach as a logical, step-by-step
roadmap. The workshop will guide learners through the core progression of the approach: starting with establishing Potential Gross Income (PGI), accounting for vacancy and collection losses, and isolating the critical Net Operating Income (NOI).
Once the NOI is determined, we will shift to then bridge between income and value: the capitalization
rate. Students will learn how to analyze market data, interpret risk, and apply rates accurately to convert a property's income into a defensible estimate of market value.
The case study will give the student the opportunity to utilize what is learned by performing a detailed
analysis of a chosen subject property.
At the end of the workshop each student will have gained insight and practical experience that can be
implemented in the workplace.
Valuation of Auto & RV Dealerships
September 16, 2026  9:00 a.m. - 4:00 p.m.
Instructor: John Zukowski, IAO, MAI, SRA
6 CE credits
Automobile and
recreational vehicle dealerships are complex commercial properties combining showrooms, offices, service facilities, parts departments, vehicle display areas, storage yards, and sometimes excess land. Their value may be influenced by location, highway exposure,
franchise requirements, manufacturer image programs, site configuration, environmental concerns, and changing vehicle-retailing trends.
This six-hour seminar examines dealership valuation from the perspective of assessors and appraisers.
Participants will learn to analyze the physical and operational differences among automobile, RV, used-car, and specialty dealerships. Particular attention will be given to separating real property from vehicle inventory, equipment, trade fixtures, franchise
rights, goodwill, and business enterprise value.
The seminar applies the cost, sales comparison, and income capitalization approaches to dealership properties.
Topics include highest and best use, land and building analysis, functional and external obsolescence, comparable-sale selection, dealership leases, sale-leasebacks, market rent, capitalization rates, and excess land. Practical case studies will demonstrate
how to develop, reconcile, document, and defend a credible dealership valuation.
Amish Property Valuation
October 21, 2026  9:00 a.m. - 4:00 p.m.
Instructor: John Zukowski, IAO, MAI, SRA
6 CE credits
In this seminar, we explore non-traditional residential and commercial property types. Because of religious
reasons or traditional reasons, some property types are built without some modern utilities or do not utilize these when they exist. This often creates a deficiency in the traditional market (Functional Obsolescence) or a Superadequacy to the nontraditional
purchaser.
We will research the concept of value to whom and how this fits in with the Market Value definition,
and within the concept of Current Use. From there we will explore the three approaches to value. This seminar will wrap up with a hands-on case study, so bring a calculator. This seminar should be informative to all rural assessors and appraisers; it is an
all-level class for entry-level to advanced.
Agricultural Exemption Processing
October 26, 2026  9:00 a.m. - 4:00 p.m.
Instructor: Stephen Harris, CCD
6 CE credits
This in-depth class will discuss and review the nuances of effectively administering the Agricultural Land assessment (exemption) program. It will cover
the differences between land located in an Agricultural District and Committed land outside an Agricultural District. The class will review the required initial documentation in order to determine eligibility, as well as the calculations to arrive at an exemption
amount, both manually and within RPSV4. Also discussed will be the yearly renewal process and penalties for conversions with the appropriate calculations.
Mastering the Cost Approach
October 30, 2026  9:00 a.m. - 4:00 p.m.
Instructor: Edye McCarthy, FIAO
6 CE credits
This seminar will be a comprehensive, 6-hour course designed to go from economic theory to practical, hands-on application. The
seminar will be broken into 4 segments: vacant land valuation, estimating new construction costs using industry-standard methods, and navigating the complex math behind physical, functional, and external depreciation.  By combining the above with many exercises,
this seminar will equip the assessor with a step-by-step toolkit to confidently calculate and reconcile property values for new construction and special use properties.
Continuing Education Hours/Re-Certification Credits
Eligible assessors and county directors who attend NYSAA classes will receive education credit and
reimbursement from ORPTS, pursuant to their rules. The Institute of Assessing Officers will award six (6) re-certification
credits to all Institute members who attend one-day seminars.
None of the above classes are eligible for DOS credit.

As assessors, our responsibility is different. We do not write the law or determine the policy behind it, nor is our role to decide whether an exemption is fair or appropriate. Our
responsibility is to understand the law as enacted and administer it accurately, consistently, and professionally.
Please note: The information presented will reflect the law and available guidance
as understood at the time of the webinar. Additional guidance from ORPTS, subsequent legislative action, or other developments may affect how the exemption is ultimately administered. NYSAA will continue to provide updates to its membership as additional information
becomes available.
This webinar is intended to help assessors better understand the legislation, the perspective of the veterans it affects, and the issues surrounding its implementation as we prepare
to administer the changes to RPTL §458-a.
Scott Shedler, IAO, will also provide some relevant updates as it relates to assessors and the small claims assessment review (SCAR).  This promises to be a very informative webinar.
No CE credit is awarded for webinars.
As always, at the conclusion of the webinar, one lucky member will win a $25 gift card. You must be present to win.
One-Day Seminars
Income Approach Case Study
September 9, 2026  9:00 a.m. - 4:00 p.m.
Instructor: Edye McCarthy, FIAO
6 CE credits
Understanding how a property generates income is often the truest key to unlocking its actual value.
The Income Approach: Demystifying the math and methodology, is a comprehensive workshop designed to demystify the mechanics of income capitalization and present tools to confidently value
income-producing properties. This workshop approaches valuation from the ground up, treating the Income Approach as a logical, step-by-step roadmap. The workshop will guide learners through the core progression of the approach: starting with establishing Potential
Gross Income (PGI), accounting for vacancy and collection losses, and isolating the critical Net Operating Income (NOI).
Once the NOI is determined, we will shift to then bridge between income and value: the capitalization rate. Students will learn how
to analyze market data, interpret risk, and apply rates accurately to convert a property's income into a defensible estimate of market value.
The case study will give the student the opportunity to utilize what is learned by performing a detailed analysis of a chosen subject
property.
At the end of the workshop each student will have gained insight and practical experience that can be implemented in the workplace.
Valuation of Auto & RV Dealerships
September 16, 2026  9:00 a.m. - 4:00 p.m.
Instructor: John Zukowski, IAO, MAI, SRA
6 CE credits
Automobile and recreational vehicle dealerships are complex commercial properties combining showrooms, offices, service facilities,
parts departments, vehicle display areas, storage yards, and sometimes excess land. Their value may be influenced by location, highway exposure, franchise requirements, manufacturer image programs, site configuration, environmental concerns, and changing vehicle-retailing
trends.
This six-hour seminar examines dealership valuation from the perspective of assessors and appraisers. Participants will learn to analyze
the physical and operational differences among automobile, RV, used-car, and specialty dealerships. Particular attention will be given to separating real property from vehicle inventory, equipment, trade fixtures, franchise rights, goodwill, and business enterprise
value.
The seminar applies the cost, sales comparison, and income capitalization approaches to dealership properties. Topics include highest
and best use, land and building analysis, functional and external obsolescence, comparable-sale selection, dealership leases, sale-leasebacks, market rent, capitalization rates, and excess land. Practical case studies will demonstrate how to develop, reconcile,
document, and defend a credible dealership valuation.
Amish Property Valuation
October 21, 2026  9:00 a.m. - 4:00 p.m.
Instructor: John Zukowski, IAO, MAI, SRA
6 CE credits
In this seminar, we explore non-traditional residential and commercial property types. Because of religious reasons or traditional
reasons, some property types are built without some modern utilities or do not utilize these when they exist. This often creates a deficiency in the traditional market (Functional Obsolescence) or a Superadequacy to the nontraditional purchaser.
We will research the concept of value to whom and how this fits in with the Market Value definition, and within the concept of Current
Use. From there we will explore the three approaches to value. This seminar will wrap up with a hands-on case study, so bring a calculator. This seminar should be informative to all rural assessors and appraisers; it is an all-level class for entry-level to
advanced.
Agricultural Exemption Processing
October 26, 2026  9:00 a.m. - 4:00 p.m.
Instructor: Stephen Harris, CCD
6 CE credits
This in-depth class will discuss and review the nuances of effectively administering the Agricultural Land assessment (exemption) program. It will cover the differences between land located in an Agricultural
District and Committed land outside an Agricultural District. The class will review the required initial documentation in order to determine eligibility, as well as the calculations to arrive at an exemption amount, both manually and within RPSV4. Also discussed
will be the yearly renewal process and penalties for conversions with the appropriate calculations.
Mastering the Cost Approach
October 30, 2026  9:00 a.m. - 4:00 p.m.
Instructor: Edye McCarthy, FIAO
6 CE credits
This seminar will be a comprehensive, 6-hour course designed to go from economic theory to practical, hands-on application. The seminar
will be broken into 4 segments: vacant land valuation, estimating new construction costs using industry-standard methods, and navigating the complex math behind physical, functional, and external depreciation.  By combining the above with many exercises, this
seminar will equip the assessor with a step-by-step toolkit to confidently calculate and reconcile property values for new construction and special use properties.
Continuing Education Hours/Re-Certification Credits
Eligible assessors and county directors who attend NYSAA classes will receive education credit and reimbursement from ORPTS, pursuant
to their rules. The Institute of Assessing Officers will award six (6) re-certification credits to all Institute members who attend one-day seminars.
None of the above classes are eligible for DOS credit.

Hello,
We are finding more than a few mistakes on deeds as they come to our office AFTER being filed.  Example, one today that showed sales price of $310,000
on the 5217, yet consideration of $700,000.  My clerk called the attorney and asked why the difference, and they realized it was a typo--should be $310,000.  We asked that they do a deed correction, and they are asking--why didn't we 'catch it'.  We said, WE
JUST DID!  We don't get to see them before they get filed.  They need to do a deed correction, as the State will flag this if we send it up AS IS.
Do you all get your deeds and 5217's AFTER they have been filed?  Do you bother reaching out to attorneys when you find mistakes?
Our town is not used to our office calling out mistakes--but we are finding a fair amount of them--as we have a new clerk who is a title searcher and knows

subject: Deed Question
body:
Hello,
We are finding more than a few mistakes on deeds as they come to our office AFTER being filed.  Example, one today that showed sales price of $310,000 on the
5217, yet consideration of $700,000.  My clerk called the attorney and asked why the difference, and they realized it was a typo--should be $310,000.  We asked that they do a deed correction, and they are asking--why didn't we 'catch it'.  We said, WE JUST DID!
We don't get to see them before they get filed.  They need to do a deed correction, as the State will flag this if we send it up AS IS.
Do you all get your deeds and 5217's AFTER they have been filed?  Do you bother reaching out to attorneys when you find mistakes?
Our town is not used to our office calling out mistakes--but we are finding a fair amount of them--as we have a new clerk who is a title searcher and knows this
stuff like the back of her hand, and our former clerk did not.  Everything basically went through as is before.
Thoughts?  T

subject: Re: Forestry rollback question
body:
When I've calculated these I just put them on as a special district move tax (like unpaid water/sewer) and they show up on the next county bill. I had one earlier this year and so it's just in there on the
parcel and will be on the tax roll in December, but I don't recalculate it for the new school taxes or anything.
Corey Metz

Sent: Monday, September 29, 2025 10:01 AM
To: RPTD@LIST-NYSAC.US
Subject: Forestry rollback question
Happy Monday, all,
I did a Forestry Rollback in April for our Finance department at the request of the DEC. All well and good and I had not heard about it again until last week, when I was asked if the final number is still
good or if it needs to be updated, I assume because now we have a new school tax rate and I guess it must not have been paid yet.
Do we chase forestry exemptions like that? If you do one, do you have to keep updating it each time there is a new tax rate until it gets paid off or cleared up? I kind of assume yes, that we use the latest
tax rates available, but it could be that no, the rollback is the same for the year no matter what month you do it in...

subject: Forestry rollback question
body:
Happy Monday, all,
I did a Forestry Rollback in April for our Finance department at the request of the DEC. All well and good and I had not heard about it again until last week, when I was asked if the final number is still
good or if it needs to be updated, I assume because now we have a new school tax rate and I guess it must not have been paid yet.
Do we chase forestry exemptions like that? If you do one, do you have to keep updating it each time there is a new tax rate until it gets paid off or cleared up? I kind of assume yes, that we use the latest
tax rates available, but it could be that no, the rollback is the same for the year no matter what month you do it in...
Paul Wiley
Director
Orange County Office of Real Property
255 Main St
Goshen, NY 10924
O: (845) 291-2494

subject: new manufactured home law
body:
CAUTION:
Good Morning,
Is anyone aware of the new law going into effect 12/12 regarding converting manufactured homes from personal property to real property and how this process will shake out?  I believe our Clerks Office plans on sending the assessors the
"affidavit of affixation" for them to adjust the property's value if necessary similar to them sending the 5217's.  If a manufactured home is leased they would need the land owners consent to convert it but that would ultimately give the land owner title to
the home and not the previous manufactured home owner.  Issues also could arise when they wish to sell the home because an actual deed will need to be filed along with a legal description which would require someone to go through the subdivision process/survey/etc.
Paul
https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/bills/2025/S7120
Paul G. Romano, CCD, Director

subject: Re: BAR Decisions and changing assessments
body:
CAUTION:
No.
Each roll year stands alone when you are talking about board of assessment review.
The tax payer can only grieve the current year.
There is a freeze for the following year if the assessment is reduced in a SCAR proceeding and a three year freeze for a tax cert.
Real Property Tax
§  739. Prohibition against change in assessment following decision in
small claims proceeding.  1. Except as hereinafter provided  and  except
as  to  any  parcel  of real property located within a special assessing
unit as defined in article eighteen of this chapter, where the  decision
of  a  small claims hearing officer orders a reduction in an assessment,
the  assessed  valuation  contained  in  such  decision  shall  not   be
thereafter  changed  on  such  property  for  the  next  assessment roll
prepared on the basis of the taxable status date next  occurring  on  or
after the taxable status date of the most recent assessment under review
in  the  proceeding  subject to such final order or judgment.  Where the
assessor or other local official  having  custody  and  control  of  the
assessment  roll  receives notice of the order or judgment subsequent to
the filing of the next assessment roll, he  or  she  is  authorized  and
directed  to  correct  the entry of assessed valuation on the assessment
roll to conform to the provisions of this section.
2. An assessment on property subject to the provisions of  subdivision
one of this section may be changed on an assessment roll where:
(a)  There  is  a  revaluation  or  update of all real property on the
assessment roll;
(b) There is a revaluation or update in a special  assessing  unit  of
all real property of the same class;
(c) There has been a physical change (improvement) to the property;
(d) The zoning of such property has changed;
(e) Such property has been altered by fire, demolition, destruction or
similar catastrophe;
(f)  An  action  has been taken by any office of the federal, state or
local government which caused a discernible change in the  general  area
where the property is located which directly impacts on property values;
(g)  The  owner  of  the  property  becomes  eligible or ineligible to
receive an exemption; or
(h) The use or classification of the property has changed.
3. No petition for review of the assessment of such property shall  be
filed  while  the provisions of subdivisions one and two of this section
are applicable to such property.
Real Property Tax
§  727. Prohibition against change in assessment following litigation.
1. Except as hereinafter provided, and except as to any parcel  of  real
property  located  within a special assessing unit as defined in article
eighteen of this chapter where an assessment being reviewed pursuant  to
this   article   is   found   to  be  unlawful,  unequal,  excessive  or
misclassified by final court order or judgment, the  assessed  valuation
so  determined shall not be changed for such property for the next three
succeeding assessment rolls prepared on the basis of the  three  taxable
status  dates  next occurring on or after the taxable status date of the
most recent assessment under review in the proceeding  subject  to  such
final  order  or  judgment.   Where the assessor or other local official
having custody and control of the assessment roll receives notice of the
order or judgment subsequent to the filing of the next assessment  roll,
he  or  she  is authorized and directed to correct the entry of assessed
valuation on the assessment roll to conform to the  provisions  of  this
section.
2.  An assessment on property subject to the provisions of subdivision
one of this section may be changed on an assessment roll where:
(a) There is a revaluation or update  of  all  real  property  on  the
assessment roll;
(b)  There  is  a revaluation or update in a special assessing unit of
all real property of the same class;
(c) There has been a physical change (improvement) to the property;
(d) The zoning of such property has changed;
(e) Such property has been altered by fire, demolition, destruction or
similar catastrophe;
(f) An action has been taken by any office of the  federal,  state  or
local  government  which caused a discernible change in the general area
where the property is located which directly impacts on property values;
(g) There has been a change  in  the  occupancy  rate  of  twenty-five
percent  or  greater  in  a  building located on a property which is not
eligible for an assessment review under  title  one-A  of  this  article
(small claims assessment review);
(h)  The  owner  of  the  property  becomes  eligible or ineligible to
receive an exemption; or
(i) The use or classification of the property has changed.
3.  No petition for review of the assessment on such property shall be
filed while the provisions  of  subdivision  one  of  this  section  are
applicable to such property.
